title: 6 Figure Creative: Remote High-Ticket Closer
description:
Headquarters: Nashville, Tennessee, United States
URL: https://6figurecreative.com/podcast/
This position offers $100K guaranteed minimum with uncapped commissions selling a $6,400 business consulting offer to leads who were generated primarily through Meta ads
Please do not apply unless you can provide real numbers from your previous sales roles.
During the interview process, be prepared to walk us through how many calls you took, how many sales you made, what the offer cost, where the leads came from, how much revenue you personally closed, and exactly how your close rate was calculated.
-----
Dear future sales rep,
We're searching for someone who is incredible at turning skeptical strangers into clients by truly understanding what is happening in their business, helping them see what needs to change, and guiding them through the fears and objections keeping them stuck.
Most of our prospects first discover us through Meta ads. By the time they reach your calendar, they have applied to speak with us and have some familiarity with our company, but most are still cold or lukewarm.
You will need to earn their trust.
You will need to diagnose the real problem.
You will need to help qualified prospects make a clear decision instead of letting them run back to the same habits that have kept their business stuck for years.
This role is a top priority at 6 Figure Creative because our entire company exists to help creative freelancers solve one giant problem:
They have no idea where their next client is coming from.
Everything we do is designed to help them solve that problem permanently by building a repeatable client acquisition system.
We're an established, profitable company doing roughly $2.5 million in annual revenue, with a consistent paid acquisition engine generating sales opportunities primarily through Meta ads.
We know there is significantly more upside available with the right person in this seat, so we're looking for a proven closer who can help us raise the bar for the entire sales team.
Why we are offering a $100K guaranteed minimum
Most remote sales jobs throw out a giant OTE number, give you no guarantee whatsoever, and make you absorb all the risk of joining a company you have never worked with before.
We are doing something different.
We want someone with a real, documented track record who already has other options.
We also understand that joining a smaller sales team is a risk. You do not know yet how good our leads are, how strong the offer is, how the company operates, or whether the opportunity is as good as we say it is.
So we are taking most of that downside off your plate.
You will receive a guaranteed minimum of $100,000 per year while keeping the full upside of our existing uncapped commission structure.
To be completely clear, this is not a $100,000 salary plus commissions.
Each month, you receive whichever amount is greater:
$8,333.33 in guaranteed compensation
The commissions you earned that month
There is no negative draw balance.
You never owe the guarantee back.
If your commissions exceed the guarantee, you receive the higher commission amount.
The guarantee does not mean the performance standard is lower. It means we are willing to take a real financial risk to attract someone capable of raising it.
If you are looking for a comfortable $100,000 job where you can close 15% of your calls and hide, this is not that job.
If you perform at the level your track record suggests, the guaranteed minimum should eventually stop mattering because your commissions will be higher.
What You'll Do
As our Remote High-Ticket Closer, your primary responsibility is converting qualified prospects into clients for our 90-Day Client Acquisition Consulting Sprint.
You will conduct consultative enrollment calls over Zoom, diagnose the prospect's business challenges, determine whether they are a strong fit, clearly explain how we can help, and confidently ask qualified prospects to enroll.
These are not random cold calls.
The prospects have applied to speak with us, but most were originally generated through paid Meta ads and will not arrive fully sold.
Once a prospect lands on your calendar, you own that opportunity from preparation through follow-up and final decision.
Your main responsibilities include:
1: Enrollment calls:
You will spend most of your time helping prospects determine whether our consulting sprint is right for them.
If they truly need our help and are a strong fit, you should see it as your responsibility to help them make the decision instead of allowing fear, uncertainty, or a weak objection to send them back to the same situation they wanted to escape.
That means you will:
Review every application before the call
Diagnose the real issues inside the prospect's business
Understand their goals, urgency, financial situation, and readiness
Determine whether they are a strong fit for our consulting sprint
Clearly explain our process, expectations, and investment
Make a direct recommendation when you believe they should enroll
Handle objections with empathy, patience, and confidence
Disqualify prospects who are not a good fit
Avoid enrolling obvious red-flag or high-risk clients just to hit a sales number
2: CRM and lead ownership
You will take complete ownership of every lead assigned to you inside GoHighLevel.
No qualified opportunity should be lost because of weak follow-up, incomplete notes, or an unclear next step.
That means you will:
Keep every opportunity stage accurate
Complete detailed notes after every call
Record the outcome and next step for every prospect
Complete all required follow-up on time
Reschedule qualified prospects who miss their calls
Work no-shows through our recovery process
Continue following up until the prospect enrolls, declines, or is formally closed out
Keep your sales data accurate enough that we never have to guess what is happening inside your pipeline
3: Call review and improvement
Every enrollment call is recorded.
You should already be excellent at sales when you join us. Call review here is about sharpening strong performance, identifying patterns, testing better approaches, and turning individual wins into improvements the entire sales team can use.
You will regularly review your own calls, participate in team call reviews and roleplay, and bring useful insights from your conversations back to the rest of the company.
That means you will:
Review your own calls and identify specific areas to improve
Bring useful wins, losses, and difficult calls to team call reviews
Give and receive direct, thoughtful feedback
Test new approaches instead of relying on the same script forever
Apply what we learn to future calls
Help identify patterns in objections, lead quality, messaging, and offer positioning
Share what is working so the entire sales team improves alongside you
4: Improve the company's sales process
You will work closely with me, the founder, to continuously improve our offer, messaging, scripts, follow-up, and overall sales process.
You are talking directly to the market every day. That makes your feedback extremely valuable.
You will help us:
Identify recurring objections and concerns
Find weaknesses in our messaging or offer
Improve our enrollment call structure
Improve email and text follow-up
Reduce the time between the first call and the final decision
Share useful insights with our marketing and consulting teams
Build a stronger sales system for everyone who joins after you
What Success In This Role Looks Like
We are hiring someone who can raise the bar, not just hit the current one.
Within six months, the expectation is that you are handling approximately 70 to 80 completed sales calls per month and maintaining a 30% or greater close rate.
A 35% or greater close rate would be exceptional.
We expect a fast ramp:
9 or more new clients in your first full production month
12 or more in your second full production month
15 or more in your third full production month
Your first-year target is at least 225 new clients, with 250 or more as the goal.
Who you'll work with
You will report directly to me (Brian Hood), the founder and person writing this job description.
You will also work alongside a veteran closer who has been with the company for 3+ years.
We are not a 40-person boiler room where you are handed a script, dropped into a Slack channel, and treated like rep number 37.
You will have direct access to the person who can actually change the offer, marketing, script, follow-up process, or sales system when something is not working.
See what you'd be selling
This role is easier to evaluate when you can see the actual offer and the proof behind it.
Review the Clients By Design program overview
See what clients have produced from their paid-ad campaigns
Why apply for this job?
If you're an experienced sales rep who wants to use your skills to help transform the lives of creatives who run freelance businesses, this job might be the perfect fit for you.
Our clients include Grammy-winning music producers, designers, videographers, and other creative freelancers.
Despite being extremely talented at their craft, they have never been taught how to consistently find and close clients.
The decision you help them make on a sales call can completely change their career.
Not only will you be affecting the lives and businesses of the people you enroll in our consulting program, but you'll also be impacting each and every client they work with as well.
If you're a high performer who's been stuck in a toxic sales team and you want to help create a healthy, thriving sales culture, you'll love being able to help us build out the sales team from the ground up and set the right culture from day one.
If you've spent years selling products you don't believe in , this is an opportunity to use your talent on something that genuinely helps people build better businesses and lives.
If you are tired of being one of dozens of closers with no influence over anything upstream, you will have direct access to the founder and a real voice in how we improve the company.
If you want the upside of commission without gambling your income while learning a completely new company, offer, and lead source, that is exactly why we created the guaranteed minimum.
Where you'll work
Our entire company operates remotely, with a diverse team spread across the United States, Portugal, England, Romania, Israel, and South Korea.
You can work from home, a quiet coworking space, or anywhere else with reliable internet and a professional place to take calls.
You must be available to take calls during U.S. business hours and have a setup where prospects will not hear dogs barking, roommates yelling, or a coffee grinder running during their enrollment call.
What We Do At 6 Figure Creative (And Why We Do It)
6 Figure Creative is a business consultancy for creative freelancers who are stuck relying on referrals, word of mouth, inconsistent content, or last-minute desperate outreach to find clients.
Our mission is to help creatives earn more without selling their souls.
Our 90-Day Client Acquisition Consulting Sprint helps freelancers build and implement a repeatable system for attracting and closing clients.
We believe that the education system is fundamentally broken. Universities will gladly charge their students $100k+ for a creative degree and never teach them the most important skills and strategies for how to actually get an ROI from their investment.
The consulting program you'll be selling exists to help the best creatives in the world change the trajectory of their careers (and lives) by learning the skills universities failed to teach them.
It takes more than passion to succeed, and everything we do is built around giving our clients the strategies, tools, processes, guidance, consulting, and accountability they need to have successful businesses.
If this sounds like the opportunity you've been looking for, apply below.
I look forward to working with you

title: Donât Put Yourself a Box
description:
Photo by Piotr MusioÅ / Unsplash
Donât Put Yourself in a Box
Personal Development and Career Growth
Apr 26, 2024
Summary
Companies need "boxes" (job classifications) to grow and function. This makes hiring, compensation, and career development tractable, and promotes fair treatment of employees.
If the boxes are too large, a company can't grow. If the boxes are too small, innovation and ownership are smothered.
The size of a company's boxes is directly proportional to the level of trust employees have for management.
To get hired, put yourself in the box the company is hiring for. Tailor your resume to highlight those skills and experiences; put yourself out there as a âspecialistâ in the thing theyâre hiring for.
If aiming for a promotion, demonstrate how your work embodies the behaviors and impacts of the next-level âboxâ.
Don't let those boxes define you. Your value and identity goes far beyond any job description.
Hot Take
Businesses can't function at scale unless they put people in standardized "boxes"; if you want to be hired and to grow your career, you need to understand that, and understand how to work with those boxes. On the other hand, you can't be reduced to a box, and if you tie your identity to those boxes in your thinking, you'll limit yourself in ways that are unnatural and harmful.
This is like the paradox of SchrÃ¶dinger's Cat, both alive and dead at the same time. Like with quantum mechanics and the cat, whether youâre in a box or not depends on whoâs doing the measuring: your employer, or you.
My Box Origin Story
My introduction to the idea of âboxesâ came in the late 2000s, when I noticed that people at Google were having a hard time getting hired or promoted if they were doing âoperationalâ work that didnât involve much traditional program management. Whether they were being considered for hiring or promotion, they were told, essentially, â Youâve done some great work, but itâs not program management; weâre not sure what role/ladder is a fit for you, but itâs not this one. Next! â
This was clearly a problemâeven though they didnât do PERT diagrams and Gantt charts, Googlers did important work in these roles, and roadblocks to hiring and promoting them created both operational and retention issues as jobs went vacant and high-performing employees felt their value wasnât being recognized. As a member of both Program Management hiring and promotion committees at Google I had more visibility to this issue than most others; I spoke to a friend of mine in People Operations (Googleâs HR), who turned out to already be well aware of this problem from repeatedly dealing with upset hiring managers and frustrated promotion candidates. Together, we hatched a plan: to create a new job ladder (job classification) for these âoperationalâ program managers to move to, that was better suited to the type of work they did.
We gathered some data, wrote a proposal, and set up a meeting with the SVP responsible for all engineering at Google. The SVP had been in quite a few meetings Iâd presented to before; I knew him to be not only a brilliant and capable leader, but a genuinely nice guy, too, so I had no worries about the meeting. Imagine my shock then, when this âgenuinely nice guyâ started yelling at us, telling my partner and I that we were going to wreck Google culture!
I vividly remember what he said: â DONâT PUT PEOPLE IN BOXES! â He told us Google needed some job classifications, but that our culture required those classifications to be both broad and vague so both employees and their managers wouldnât be blocked from doing whatever needed to be done. The worst thing we could do, the SVP told us, was to make the classification âboxesâ so small people could say â thatâs not my job ââwhich is precisely what he saw us proposing to do!
A year or two before this Google had shifted from having just three job types (over-broadly, they were â engineers â, â technical people that donât do engineering â, and â everyone else â) to having around around a dozen (one of which was my ladder, âTechnical Program Managersâ). There had been a lot of debate about whether those boxes were already too smallâ¦ but the senior team had decided 12â15 job categories were acceptableâenough large boxes to make hiring, career development, and compensation more efficient, but not so many that jobs were defined too narrowly. We left his office dejected, but also enlightened: it said a lot to me that this SVP thought it so important to Googleâs culture, a lesson Iâve never forgotten. (Times have changed though; Google now has many more job ladders, including at least 5â10 âoperationalâ ladders broken off from Program Management well beyond what my friend and I had proposed).
Why Companies Need Boxes
Why do we need âboxesâ (job classifications) at all? Wouldnât the world be better if everyone just did whatever they saw that needed doing? The value of boxes to corporations comes down to two things: scaling and trust .
Scaling
If youâre in a small startup, you want employees who can wear many hats, and who wonât feel limited by things like job titles. Because there are so few employees, and because you know everyone personally and need everyone you hire to have an outsized impact, you can afford to put a lot of energy into every individual hiring decision. Compensation planning is pretty lightweight and customized, both because there arenât many people to deal with, and because you want to compensate people based on their contribution to the business, regardless of what their title is. Everyone is a âspecial snowflakeâ.
That changes quickly as your startup growsâyou cross a line where it becomes infeasible to treat every hire as a unique individual, with bespoke hiring and compensation. This is where âboxesâ become necessary: you have to put people into categories, with standards for how hiring, compensation, and career progression work for each boxâitâs the only way you can scale the company. The alternative to this would be to allow an increasing number of managers to continue bespoke hiring and comp within their own areasâ¦ which leads to the second issue, trust.
Trust
Because startups are so risky, the ability of potential employees to trust the founders is a big dealâif they donât appear trustworthy, theyâre not going to attract the kind of people they need. As the company grows, the number of managers that both employees and senior management need to trust grows, too. At some point it becomes too much: employeesâ willingness to âhave faithâ that managers will make fair and appropriate decisions drops lower and lower, so much so that everything will fall apart without the enforced fairness of standardized boxes.
ð¡
The size of the boxes in a company are directly proportional to the amount of trust employees have in management
Labor unions are the endgame for this sort of trust problem. One of the big rallying points for companies trying to avoid unionization is always to try to convince employees that management has their best interests at heart, and can be trusted. As a rule, unions have close to zero trust for management, andâas a direct consequenceâunions often push for the smallest âboxesâ possible: boxes for very narrow roles, subdivided by seniority, and sometimes further subdivided by location. They see this as the best way to ensure fairness in an environment where management canât be trusted at all . This is the ultimate version of the cultural harm my SVP was worried about.
Boxes and Hiring
Scaling and trust drive companies to put employees into standard categories, or boxes. How do those boxes affect hiring, and, understanding this, how can you better âsellâ yourself as a candidate for jobs?
Most companies above startup size need to hire for boxes, for the reasons given above; itâs just too much work to do anything else. It would be wonderful if recruiters, interviewers, and hiring managers had the time to carefully read and savor every resume that came in, and then spend time meeting with every candidate to pull out nuances that didnât come across clearly in their job histories. Thatâs not the world we live in, though; there are too many candidates to get through, and too few hours in the day.
The usual practice is for recruiters to work with hiring managers to identify standard requirements (boxes, again!) that can be used to screen out people and reduce the number of candidates they need to go into more depth with (hiring managers will usually never see any of those dropped candidates). Those standard requirements are typically based on a template used for all jobs of the same ladder and level, extended with custom specs tailored to the particular role being hired for. In the language Iâve been using in this article, the job requirements are a very clear âboxâ, and the screening process only lets through candidates whose âshapesâ fit that box, like a childâs sorting toy.
Source: Flickr user rosipaw, CC BY-NC-SA 2.0
When there are lots of candidates for a tiny number of jobs, the recruiters donât magically get more time to handle the extra candidatesâinstead, they often deal with the overload by tightening the screening criteria even further: that is, by making the boxes smaller.
Behaviorally, the shift from âstartupâ to âbig companyâ, and the shift from rapid growth to slow growth, show up to candidates as employers become increasingly selective. Startups like generalists; big companies like specialists . If there are few people vying for each job, hiring managers won't care as much about past experience; if there are many candidates, theyâll only be interested in people whoâve previously done the same kind job theyâre hiring for . These trends are amplified when business is tough and hiring budgets are thin: hiring managers become nervous about using their scarce headcount on unproven candidatesâ they need people who have already shown success in exactly the job the manager needs done .
ð¡
Iâm writing this in April, 2024, in a time of high interest rates and widespread layoffs in tech, and when there are lots of AI-based screening tools being offered that promise to save recruiters time; you do the math about the current hiring marketâ¦
Besides being lucky, there are two powerful ways to cut through âsmall box screeningâ:
Put yourself in the box theyâre hiring for. This means customizing your resume for each job you apply for, or at least for each type of job youâre going after. If theyâre hiring for someone with experience doing X, focus your resume on how youâve been successful doing X (or at least, things like X) in the past. When a recruiter or hiring manager looks at your resume, you want them to jump out of their chair and exclaim: âwow, this person is exactly what weâve been looking for!â
Pull a Kobayashi Maru by bypassing the whole screening process: use your network of personal connections to get an introduction to the hiring manager. This is probably the single most powerful thing you can do because it exposes you to the hiring manager as a whole person, instead of a peg that fits in a box.
Boxes and Promotions
A similar situation arises with promotions: the people making decisions about whether you should be promoted or not donât (usually) have the familiarity with you, or the time, to make a customized decisionâ¦ and doing so would create fairness issues. Instead, they look at whether you fit the next-level box . I want to talk about two parts to this: one related to the job ladder, and one related to the level.
Job Ladder
I vividly remember one promotion committee I served on, where we were deciding whether or not to promote an individual who had unquestionably performed at the next levelâ¦ but the work theyâd done wasnât consistent wit

title: SaaS Product Support Jedi
description:
We’re on the hunt for a sharp, self-driven SaaS pro who’s as comfortable troubleshooting API and integrations as they are navigating human conversations.
Our European client base is growing fast and we need someone who can keep up. Our software isn’t your average plug-and-play; it has a steep learning curve so you’ll need to be technically savvy while also being the kind of person clients genuinely enjoy talking to. If you’ve got SaaS in your DNA, thrive in async/remote environments, and can juggle multiple threads without breaking a sweat — keep reading.
The role
You’ll join a lean, high-performing global support team working across two SaaS products, Award Force and Good Grants. Day to day you’ll be communicating with colleagues and clients across countries, cultures, and time zones.
Support happens across email tickets, phone, and 1-1 Zoom calls. Once you’ve leveled up on product knowledge, you’ll run onboarding sessions and client meetings covering issue resolution, best practices, and product adoption.
You’ll also be hands-on with bug testing and reporting, feeding considered feedback to our product teams— always pushing to make our products better.
We have a startup mindset. We experiment with new tools, iterate on processes, and move fast. Got a great idea? Pitch it. We’re not big on bureaucracy, only results. We don’t expect you to be a slave to your chair but flexibility is a must.
You’ll need to tick these boxes
You’re based in the UTC +1 or +2 timezone range. This is non-negotiable. Our European team and clients operate in this window and we don’t allow shift work. If you live outside this range, this one’s not for you
2+ years of professional experience, ideally in a SaaS support or client-facing role
Native-level English fluency (bilingual? Even better!)
Terms like HTML, CSS, JS, API, integrations, dev console, staging & production environments, GitHub repos, and database queries don’t make you flinch. You don’t need to write code, but you need to get it
You’ve got exceptional interpersonal and communication skills—written and verbal
Client calls energise you. Four to five Zoom meetings a day? Bring it on
You’re a natural problem solver who loves helping others untangle theirs
Your writing is clean, well-structured, and detail-oriented
You’re curious by nature and love learning new things
You’re not allergic to upselling or fielding “sales-y” questions
You’re organised and process-driven. Multiple tools for different workflows? No problem — you thrive in that setup
You’re self-motivated and independent, but you also value being part of a tight-knit team
Remote work isn’t just something you dabble in—it’s where you do your best work. You’ve got fast, reliable internet and a distraction-free workspace ready to go
Responsibilities
Product support
Go deep on product knowledge through self-driven learning—become the expert
Be the first point of contact on all inbound support via email/tickets, phone, and eventually live chat
Run 1-1 Zoom sessions with clients for technical consultation and query resolution
Maintain our consistently impressive first-reply-time metric (yeah, we’re proud of it)
Provide technically accurate responses backed by hands-on testing of scenarios
Collaborate with engineering to squash bugs and keep clients in the loop with timely updates
Spot patterns in user issues and flag them for product improvement
Be seriously good with clients
Speed matters. Respond quickly and decisively
Listen deeply—get to the root of the issue and own it until it’s resolved
Treat every client interaction with genuine respect and appreciation
Build trusting, long-term relationships rooted in honesty and transparency

title: Tier 2 Member Support Agent
description:
PadSplit is a pioneering real estate platform operating in the shared housing industry, committed to providing affordable housing accommodations for low-income earners. We are dedicated to helping solve the affordable housing crisis while leveraging housing as a vehicle for financial empowerment for our members. Our principles are Care, Show it, Prove it, and weâve been proving it through our actions since 2018.
We are on a mission to change the world â one room at a time. Join us!
Learn more about PadSplit here
The Role We Need:
As a member of the escalations team, you are considered a senior member of the Customer Experience organization. This role involves handling more complex or escalated inquiries that require a higher level of expertise and customer service finesse. Advocates in this position need to be proactive problem-solvers equipped with a strong understanding of our policies, procedures, and the unique needs of our members. By collaborating closely with other departments and utilizing feedback, they contribute to refining our support processes and enhancing the overall member experience.
The Person We Are Looking For:
The ideal person should have a knack for problem-solving, especially in situations that require thoughtful analysis and a careful approach. Exceptional communication skills are essential, as the role involves conveying information clearly and confidently to our members while resolving their issues. We're looking for someone who thrives in a collaborative environment, works well across teams, and can actively contribute to improving our support processes. Above all, the ideal candidate is committed to creating a positive experience that builds trust and satisfaction among our members.
Hereâs What Youâll Do Day-To-Day:
Act as the main escalation point for complex Member support issues that need effective critical thinking, research, and problem-solving abilities
Manage a range of complex cases, such as policy-related inquiries, financial disputes, platform issues, and membership matters
Assume responsibility for cases from beginning to end, ensuring a prompt and satisfactory resolution
Serve as the representative of PadSplit, ensuring that all interactions are conducted with empathy, professionalism, and efficiency
Develop innovative solutions for the unique challenges that arise, balancing both member needs and company policies
Assist and educate members about our platform, policies, and product offerings, ensuring they fully understand their options
Maintain an in-depth understanding of our ever-evolving web and mobile products, processes, and policies
Identify recurring issues and trends, offering insights and suggestions for process and policy improvements to enhance the Member experience
Serve as the voice of the customer, advocating for members’ needs and supporting ongoing improvements in our Customer Experience (CX) operations
Collaborate closely with other teams, such as Product, Operations, and Host Support, to guarantee a seamless experience for our Members
Assume responsibility for special projects within the Customer Experience team, contributing to process enhancements and operational efficiency
Hereâs What Youâll Need To Be Successful:
Comfortable working in a fast-paced, ever-evolving environment where priorities can shift quickly
Able to stay composed under pressure while handling complex Member interactions
Strong verbal and written communication skills, ensuring clarity and professionalism in every interaction
Ability to break down complex topics and explain them in a clear, concise, and empathetic manner
A natural problem-solver who can analyze information, investigate issues, and think critically to resolve complex Member concerns
Ability to develop creative solutions while balancing Member needs and company policies
Energized by customer interactions, with a genuine passion for helping others and enhancing the Member experience
Skilled at balancing empathy with firmness, ensuring fair and effective resolutions
Ability to prioritize multiple tasks, manage workloads efficiently, and meet response time expectations
Highly detail-oriented and capable of tracking cases through resolution
Comfortable navigating multiple systems, online platforms, and support tools
Able to quickly adapt to new technologies, processes, and policy changes
Possesses a strong sense of intellectual curiosity, eager to learn, adapt, and improve
A collaborative team player with a positive, "can-do" attitude, always ready to support colleagues and contribute to team success
The Interview Process:
Your application will be reviewed for possible next steps by the Hiring Manager
If you meet eligibility requirements, the next step would be a video interview with a member of the PeopleOps team for about thirty (30) minutes
If warranted, the next step would be a video panel interview with our Tier 2 Member Support Team Leads at PadSplit for one (1) hour. For this interview, the candidate would execute a live writing assessment
If warranted, the next step would be a video interview with our Manager of T2 Member Support for forty (40) minutes. For this interview, we will assess your overall fit with a set of role-related questions
If warranted, we move to offer!
Notice to Applicants:
PadSplit participates in E-Verify. All new employees are required to complete an I-9 form and be authorized to work in the United States. Employment is contingent upon successful completion of the E-Verify process.
We are interested in every qualified candidate who is eligible to work in the United States. However, we are not able to sponsor visas.
PadSplit is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or status as a protected veteran.
We may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support parts of the hiring process, such as reviewing applications, analyzing resumes, or assessing responses and identifying potential inconsistencies or verification signals in application materials based on available information. These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. If you would like more information about how your data is processed, please contact us.
Compensation is based on the role's scope, national market benchmarks, the person's expertise and experience, and the impact of their contributions to our business goals.

title: Social Media Coordinator
description:
Help grow an independent magazine dedicated to investigative journalism, culture and ideas.
Clandestine Magazine is looking for a Social Media Manager on a part-time voluntary basis to help grow our social media presence and introduce our work to new audiences.
We are an independent volunteer-led publication covering the stories, ideas and cultural movements shaping our world.
We are not a conventional magazine. Our editorial landscape spans 12 topics â
Affairs â World Affairs, Cities, Environment, Philosophy, Politics and the Progressive World.
Culture â Art, Fashion, Film, Literature, Music and Technology.
Alongside our core features, we publish investigative reporting, immersive gonzo journalism, long-form essays and showcase emerging artists.
As a volunteer-led publication, we're building something with purpose. Beyond journalism, we also support charitable initiatives including a community kitchen and projects supporting people experiencing homelessness.
The Role
You'll take ownership of our social media strategy and help build a distinctive, recognisable presence that reflects the quality of our journalism and creative work.
Responsibilities include:
Developing and executing an Instagram & Tiktok content strategy.
Creating engaging posts, carousels, stories and reels.
Planning and maintaining a content calendar.
Writing compelling captions aligned with our editorial voice.
Growing our audience organically through community engagement.
Identifying trends while maintaining our editorial identity.
Working with editors, writers and artists to showcase new features and projects.
Monitoring performance and suggesting ways to improve reach and engagement.
We're Looking For Someone Who
Has experience managing or growing an Instagram account (personal, professional or voluntary).
Has a strong eye for design, storytelling and visual presentation.
Understands what performs well on Instagram and Tiktok without relying on clickbait.
Is interested in journalism, culture, current affairs or the creative industries.
Is proactive, reliable and enjoys taking initiative.
Can commit a few hours each week.
What You'll Gain
A key leadership role within an ambitious independent publication.
Creative freedom to shape our social media strategy.
Opportunities to collaborate with writers, editors and artists from around the world.
Portfolio-building experience with published work and measurable growth.
About Clandestine
Explore the world â 12 topics.
Clandestine Magazine is an independent publication dedicated to investigative journalism, the cultural zeitgeist and the ideas shaping our time.
We believe in rigorous reporting, thoughtful storytelling and publishing work that is both intellectually engaging and thought-provoking. Our pages bring together investigative features, long-form essays and distinctive voices from around the world.
We are not a conventional magazine. Our editorial landscape spans 12 topics â
Affairs â World Affairs, Cities, Environment, Philosophy, Politics and the Progressive World.
Culture â Art, Fashion, Film, Literature, Music and Technology.
Alongside our core editorial, we publish 'Injustices', examining global issues, overlooked stories and the realities that often escape the headlines. 'Gonzo' features immersive, first-hand reporting, offering deeply personal perspectives on people, places and experiences, while 'Essays' provides a home for considered long-form writing and original thought. Creativity is equally central to Clandestine, and through our 'Your Art Here' section, we offer emerging and established artists a place to showcase their work, celebrating originality and the creative voices that shape the creative disciplines of today.
Beyond publishing, we are committed to supporting charitable initiatives that help those facing hardship. Kindness, compassion and respect for others remain central to our ethos, shaping both our work and the community we continue to build. We work alongside registered charities and currently run two of our own initiatives â a community kitchen providing support for those in need, and a 'Tap for the Homeless' scheme, offering a simple way to provide essential assistance to people experiencing homelessness.
More than a magazine, Clandestine is a collective of curious minds, writers, artists and readers brought together by a shared appreciation for thoughtful journalism and culture.

title: A Book of Your Own
description:
Editorâs Note: The following piece, by the late, great Herman Holtz, was to appear as part of Hermanâs âHindsights & Insightsâ column. It is part of our collection of âclassicsââarticles that stand the test of time no matter how many technologies come and go. Published with permission.
It seems, from what I read every day on the TECHWR-L list, that it isnât at all easy for most people to break into a beginning tech writing job. Of course, that kind of Catch 22âyou need a job to get the experience you need to qualify for the jobâis far from unknown, especially in the high-tech working world. Itâs why prospective employers want to see clips and other evidence that you can write reasonably well, whether it is technical or not, before they will consider you.
I was a tech writer long before I wrote my first book, although I had to jump through some difficult hoops to land my first tech writing job (a series of six tests on technology); however, a great deal of my work later, especially my consulting jobs, came about as a result of my books and the reputation they bestowed on me. Being published between covers brings you respect almost as quickly and surely as becoming known as a millionaire business owner does. Even now, it happens. A reader who owns a small business in Baltimore hired me recently to do some consulting with him, after reading one of my books published a few years ago. The gentleman had read several books on the subject of proposal writing and contracting, and he decided that my book reflected the kind of thinking he needed, although it was one of my most slender volumes.
It is really not that difficult to turn out your first book if you select a subject that you are reasonably familiar with (and so can research efficiently) and plan ahead with a solid and well-thought-out outline. Remember that what you write does not have to be a thick tome. My books have generally run to about 275 to 500 pages, but I have also written my share of books that printed out to fewer than 200 pages.
There Are Many Ways To Get Ideas For Books, And The More You Concentrate On The Need, The More New Ideas You Will Get. Here Are Just a Few Tips
Start reading the periodicals that deal with the subject Probably they will be trade journals and may touch only lightly on the subject, but that is fine. But, how much is there to say about the subject? Is it useful detailâthat is, does a lightly-covered detail justify a book of its own? The book of mine I referred to here is a small book that presents sharply-focused abstracts on what I think to be the most important topics about proposal writingâa subject on which I have written more than one large, detailed book. The little book referred to here is virtually the opposite of expanding an article or two into a book.
Browse libraries and book stores for current books on the subject Would you go about writing a book on the subject entirely differently? Would it be a better book? How? Why? Read books that devote a chapter to the subject. How about developing that chapter into a full book of its own?
Think about what that information might mean to readers and to which readers Will it help someone start or improve their business? Improve their position in some way? Make it easier to learn a given subject?
Think about the need for the information Is the subject a very popular one? Is it on how to be a better golfer, for example? Hard to lose with any good book on golf. The same for many other subjects. There is never an end to new books about the Civil War, even if you call it The War Between the States. But if you want your first book (I hope that it will be only your first) to help your business career, it is best to choose a serious business subject or other how-to book.
Finally, remember that you donât have to write the book in a day. Do a few pages each day, and you will be surprised at how soon you have a book.

title: This IS Your Dream Job
description:
Here are two questions to ask yourself: 1) when are you most content? (Not âhappyâ per se, since happy moments are fleeting. 2) Does contentment ever happen for you during the workday?
The average American worker spends 2080 hours per year on paid work. Over 30 years, that adds up to 62,400 hours. Thatâs a LOT of time to spend doing something you donât like doing.
Research also shows that people will change careers at least 7 times during their lifetime. However, career changes arenât always drastic â you can change the focus of your daily work activity without changing jobs. Sometimes incremental shiftsâsmall changes in what you do and how you do itâare the best and most satisfying way to land that dream job
The key is to concentrate on ways to shift paid job duties into activities that give you that feeling of contentment.
Grab a Sheet Of Paper And a Pencilâor Open Up Your Favorite Word Processor And Work Through The Following Steps To Come Up With Your Own Action Plan To Realize Your Dream Job
STEP 1: Think about your current job â make a list of the tasks that comprise your job. Highlight the ones you most enjoy performing in your job. Note the ones you canât stand
STEP 2: Make a list of activities youâve done in the past that you are most proud of, and that you got the most satisfaction from. These can come from previous jobs, volunteer activities, school work, or hobbies. If you loved laying out the college newspaper, but hated the organizational aspects such as chasing people down to get their content in on time, then that tells you something about the types of activities that work for you.
STEP 3: Envision your ideal job â and list the tasks that it would encompass. What basic skills involved in your ideal job could start working on today? This could be something simple â if your ideal job is to be in charge of all written communication for your organization, an area you could start working on immediately is your writing skills. Even if your current writing skills are pretty good, there is always room to work towards a higher level of achievement.
STEP 4: Now take the list of tasks and activities from steps 1 & 2 above, along with the list of skills from step 3, and group them into functions related to your job that you could concentrate on. (For example, if you are a financial analyst, but you find the grind of financial reports tedious, but you love creating charts and graphs and putting together presentations that visually demonstrate trends â your tasks and activities list could include âcreating graphs & chartsâ, and one skill that could be on your list is â Enhance MS Excel charting & graphing skillsâ .
STEP 5: Conduct some research into the training available out there that would help you to enhance the skills you outlined in step 3. This could involve a number of options â anything from volunteering with an organization in a capacity where you could practice your skills, to taking webinars, intensive workshops, certificate programs, or working toward a degree.
STEP 6: Using the information you gathered in step 5 above, get started with the training program(s) that will meet your individual needs. Remember that you can start small and fine-tune your training plan as you go along. You can also mix and match various training components â it doesnât have to be a straight path, as long as it gets you to where you want to go. Get involved with online forums and interest groups that will help you learn more about the latest techniques in your area of interest. As you spend more time learning and practicing, your skills will improve.
Never underestimate the value of volunteering without asking for additional compensationâ¦your boss and superiors will be impressed that you are interested enough to take on a project without asking for something in return. Showcase your best efforts by volunteering to work on projects that will give you a chance to demonstrate your expertise.
Land Mines to Avoid
Being your own worst enemy â downplaying your talents wonât get you noticed or into consideration for that great new project. Toot your own horn and let others know that you are good at xyz (in the example above, creating charts and graphs). Just as important, offer to help others with that task â soon you will become the resident expert, the one that others turn to for help and advice on this topic
Being finished with learning â remember learning doesnât stop because you have that framed diploma. Keep taking courses, attending seminars and staying in touch with others in your field so that you stay at the leading edge of knowledge and practice in your area of interest
Getting stuck in a rut â Sometimes it seems easier to lay low and just plod along. But you canât stay still â keep looking for new opportunities to apply your talents and showcase them in new and interesting ways.
Decide what you like (and what you donât), do your homework, work hard at new opportunities and advertise the resultsâbefore you know it, youâll be living your dream job.
Contributor: Julie Clarke, Vancouver Island University (www.pr.viu.ca/techcomm)

title: Project Management Coordinator
description:
About the role
The Project Management Coordinator role is essential for maintaining the structure and rhythm of our high level advisory work. In this position, you will support our principals as we assist a major regional logistics and transportation group through a complex transition of their operating model. You will provide the organizational support needed to ensure that our strategic recommendations are tracked, documented, and moved toward a final decision.
About Arabian Private Holdings
Arabian Private Holdings was founded on the principle that many critical business problems do not fit the traditional large firm consulting model. A board facing a succession question or a family group weighing a capital injection does not need a team of twelve associates and a hundred page methodology deck. They need experienced partners who can sit with a problem, form a rigorous view, and defend it. We take on a limited number of mandates to ensure that every client receives direct attention from the principals who are actually accountable for the outcome. Our work covers corporate strategy, governance, and operating model efficiency for significant family groups and government entities. We operate as a remote firm, choosing to prioritize the quality of our analysis over traditional office overhead.
What you will do
Coordinate project timelines and schedules to ensure that all mandate milestones are met on time.
Support our principals in gathering research and data related to the logistics sector to help form a clear view on client challenges.
Draft concise internal updates and reports regarding the progress of specific portfolio projects.
Organize and maintain project documentation to ensure all data is accurate and accessible to the team.
Monitor project risks or delays and communicate them clearly to the responsible partners.
Assist in the preparation of governance documents and strategy materials for board level presentations.
Track communication between our firm and client representatives to maintain a clear record of decisions made.
Support the refinement of client operating models by documenting current processes and proposed changes.
What we are looking for
A logical mindset and the ability to organize complex information into clear, actionable steps.
Strong writing skills with a focus on precision and the ability to communicate ideas without using corporate jargon.
A high level of attention to detail when reviewing documents and project schedules.
Curiosity about how large holding companies and regional logistics firms function at a governance level.
The ability to work independently and manage your own tasks effectively in a remote setting.
Basic familiarity with digital tools for project tracking or a strong willingness to learn our specific methods.
How we work
We operate as a fully remote firm, which allows us to focus on the clarity of our thinking rather than the logistics of an office. This model requires a high degree of professional maturity and trust. We value intellectual honesty and direct communication, where the quality of an idea is more important than the title of the person who suggests it. As an entry level member of the team, you will receive direct mentoring from our principals, gaining exposure to how significant corporate decisions are made and executed. We prioritize high impact work on a small number of mandates, ensuring that our team can remain focused on results rather than simple activity.
What the role offers
Direct involvement in high level strategy mandates for a major regional logistics and infrastructure client.
Competitive pay that is attractive for the market and reflective of the importance of this role.
A permanent, fully remote position that offers professional autonomy and flexibility.
Mentorship from experienced principals who are leaders in the fields of governance and corporate strategy.
A professional environment that values sober analysis and clear communication over corporate theater.

title: Buffer : Senior Engineer - Growth Marketing
description:
Headquarters: United States, California
URL: https://buffer.com/
About the role
We're looking for a Senior Frontend Engineer to join our Growth Marketing team. This is a hands-on engineering role building the web experiences and systems that help Buffer grow.
The work spans building features and pages across buffer.com - interactive tools, benchmarks, referral systems, conversion flows - along with the technical implementation behind them: integrations with marketing tools, analytics and tracking systems, SEO implementations, and backend logic that powers our marketing features.
We need someone who's comfortable across the full frontend scope - strong with React and modern web development, but also capable of diving into backend logic, connecting third-party APIs, debugging tracking pipelines, and figuring out what they don't know.
You'll collaborate closely with Simon (Director of Marketing), David (Senior Design Engineer), and Kate (Senior Designer). The team values pace and iteration — we ship quickly, learn from real usage, and improve as we go. But we also care about craft — noticing the UX details and maintaining standards while keeping momentum.
What you’ll do
Lead growth engineering projects, like implementing a localization framework to support international audiences, building referral program logic and attribution systems, rebuilding our tracking implementation to improve accuracy and reliability. You’ll own projects from concept to launch, working closely with marketing, design, and other engineers.
Build features on Buffer's marketing site — ship landing pages, interactive tools, and conversion flows that help people discover and try Buffer. Create benchmarks, calculators, and utility content that educate users and drive engagement.
Shape marketing platform capabilities by building systems and frameworks that let the team move faster. Create A/B testing infrastructure, develop programmatic page generation for SEO/AEO, implement content management patterns, and build reusable components that make future projects easier to ship.
Drive experimentation and optimization — implement A/B tests, optimize conversion funnels, and help the team learn faster through code. Set up experiments, validate results, and iterate based on what we learn. Balance moving quickly with maintaining quality.
Improve foundations by maintaining integrations with our marketing technology stack (Segment, GTM, Mixpanel, BigQuery), upgrading dependencies, optimizing performance, and ensuring accessibility. You'll also participate in our on-call rotation and contribute to ongoing system health — fixing bugs, addressing security vulnerabilities, and other improvements that keep buffer.com running smoothly.
Contribute to shaping engineering culture by pairing with other engineers, reviewing code, sharing knowledge about growth systems and marketing engineering patterns, and helping level up how we approach frontend work at Buffer.
Helpful skills and experience
You have strong frontend foundations — solid experience with React, TypeScript, and modern web development. Our site runs on Next.js, but we value adaptability and curiosity over specific stack experience.
You're comfortable working across the stack when needed — writing backend logic, building API routes, getting data from various external systems, and connecting third-party integrations together.
You've worked with marketing or growth teams and are comfortable with SEO, analytics, A/B testing, and conversion optimization. You've likely built referral systems, programmatic pages, or conversion funnels, and you know how to set up tracking, validate implementations, and measure impact accurately.
You're comfortable navigating ambiguity and thinking in systems — you bring clarity and ask good questions to move ideas forward even when requirements aren't fully defined. You look at the full system, understanding how different technologies and goals connect, and build things that can scale and improve holistically rather than just solving point problems.
You have a personal stake in the world of content creation, maybe you’ve run a newsletter, built an audience on social media, or regularly share your own work online. You’ve used Buffer before and care about the experience of planning, creating, and publishing content.
You balance craft with pace — you ship quickly and learn from real usage, but you also care about quality. You notice UX details, maintain accessibility standards, think about performance, and understand when to polish versus when to iterate.
You thrive in remote, async environments — you communicate clearly, support your teammates, and don't wait for permission to make progress. You work effectively across marketing, design, and engineering, and can explain technical decisions to non-technical stakeholders.
You're fluent with AI tools and use them to work with more leverage and improve your efficiency. Bonus points if you've also integrated AI into user-facing marketing features at scale (like generating personalized content, automating asset creation, or building intelligent systems).
You've likely been doing this for at least 5+ years, but depth of experience and impact matter more than a specific number of years.
Our tech stack
We use Next.js v15+ with React and TypeScript for buffer.com (currently using Pages router, planning to migrate to App router). We use Express middleware for some routing (planning to migrate to Next.js middleware).
Styling with CSS Modules and Motion for animations, and use Radix UI and Base UI for accessible components (gradually migrating to Base UI as it evolves) and data visualizations using Recharts.
Our marketing technology stack includes Segment, Google Tag Manager, Mixpanel, and BigQuery for tracking and analytics.
We pull content and data from Ghost CMS (blog), Redash, Notion, Google Sheets, and various external APIs.
Interview process
Here's what our hiring process for this role is like.
Application. When submitting your application and resume, tell us why you want to join Buffer and take your time. This is your chance to make a strong first impression.
Please note: While we have several engineering roles open, we recommend applying to only one role - just choose one that resonates with you the most. If during our review or interviews we think you'd be great for a different position, we'll re-route your application internally.
Role interview. Chat with the hiring manager and a peer engineer to understand what it takes to work at Buffer. This is an opportunity for both sides to get to know each other and determine whether our expectations align.
Code review assignment. We'll send you an asynchronous assignment to review a pull request, to help us understand how you think about code and communicate technical ideas.
Technical interviews. Interview with a couple of engineers from Buffer focused on your technical experience and approach. Additionally, for senior roles, we'll have an additional conversation about your leadership, how you work with teams, and how you approach the broader challenges that come with this level.
Meet the CEO. At the very end, you will have the opportunity to meet with Joel Gascoigne, our CEO. This is a great chance for you to gain a deeper understanding of Buffer's strategy, values, and work processes.
Collaboration period. This is experimental stage for us where you would work with us on a real project over 2 days (fully paid). The goal is to see how it feels to work in the team, both for us and for you. You'll meet a few bufferoos, we'll kickoff the project, and invite you to a Slack and you'll collaborate with the team on it.
Offer. We wrap it up with an offer and discuss the final details. We would align on the last bits before we make you part of the Buffer team
At Buffer, we value diversity of experience, and we understand that comes in many forms. We’re dedicated to adding new perspectives to the team. So, if your experience is close to what we’re looking for, please consider applying.
By submitting the application, you consent to Buffer collecting and processing your personal data for recruiting purposes, find more details in our Privacy Policy .

title: Background job monitoring
description:
Glossary/
Scheduled Jobs/
Background job monitoring
Scheduled Jobs
Background job monitoring
Background job monitoring is watching asynchronous jobs for timely completion and success signals.
What is background job monitoring?
Background job monitoring describes watching asynchronous jobs for timely completion and success signals. In reliability work, the label is useful only when it maps to a measurable check, a clear owner, and a next action when expectations break. Without that operational meaning, the phrase becomes decoration in dashboards and status updates.
Why it matters
Background job monitoring matters because teams need a precise shared meaning for watching asynchronous jobs for timely completion and success signals. Vague language turns incidents into arguments about words instead of fixes.
When everyone uses the same definition, alerts, status updates, and post-incident reviews stay aligned.
How it works
In practice, watching asynchronous jobs for timely completion and success signals shows up as a concrete signal you can measure or communicate. Operators define what good looks like, watch for deviations, and record what happened when expectations break.
The useful version of background job monitoring is operational: it changes who gets notified, what customers see, or which metric a team reviews after an incident.
Practical example
Imagine a team operating around queue worker heartbeat each minute. When observed behavior stops matching the definition of background job monitoring, the team treats that change as a reliability event with a clear owner and next step.
Common misconception
Background job monitoring requires browser scripting
That reading usually collapses distinct ideas into one slogan. Keep background job monitoring tied to observable behavior so the definition stays useful under pressure.
How Fajita handles this
Use heartbeats or success pings from workers. External HTTP monitors alone may not see queue lag.

title: Resource Manager
description:
Company Description
The Story Shack is a modern, low-overhead creative studio built to scale a brand's story. We give brands the power of an in-house creative team â without the headaches and high costs that plague the industry. We address the broken creative model by offering flexible, budget-friendly, scalable, and specialized solutions for brands.
Role Description
We're on the hunt for a sharp and dependable operator to join our scrappy, fast-growing creative studio and work directly alongside our Head of Community.
As our Resource Manager, you'll be the engine behind the scenes â running talent outreach, supporting creative resourcing, coordinating project needs, and keeping administrative tasks tight and on track. You'll help make sure every project has the right people in place at the right time, and that nothing falls through the cracks.
You'll also get exposure to the business side of a growing agency â supporting resourcing, budgeting, invoicing, and talent relationships as we continue to grow.
If you've got real experience in the agency, studio, or production world, love staying organized amid creative chaos, and want a front-row seat to how a creative company is actually run, this role was made for you.
Responsibilities
Manage daily tasks with our 300-person creative community, including administrative outreach to freelance talent such as creative directors, copywriters, directors, cinematographers, photographers, producers, designers, and more â including initial outreach, scheduling, and follow-up.
Run availability and rate checks across our talent network for upcoming projects, keeping records accurate and up to date.
Support creative resourcing with Project Managers, Account Managers, and Producers by helping match the right talent to the right projects based on skill set, client needs, availability, and budget.
Handle financial administration, including invoice monitoring, payment tracking, and flagging discrepancies.
Maintain organized, up-to-date talent and project databases.
Serve as a first point of contact for talent inquiries and applications, while helping build and maintain strong relationships across our creative community.
Qualifications
Experience in a creative agency, studio, or production environment with resourcing responsibilities.
Outstanding communication and organizational skills.
Comfortable managing multiple tasks and projects simultaneously.
Detail-oriented, especially when it comes to financials and scheduling.
A collaborative, low-ego attitude with the ability to support someone else's workflow and priorities.
Genuine interest in the advertising and film industries and building relationships with creative talent.
Familiarity with talent databases, project management tools, and invoicing/accounting software is a plus.
Existing relationships within the creative production community are a plus.

A diver will perform strictly limited âNo Decompressionâ dives at a depth no greater than 100 feet of seawater while utilizing open circuit SCUBA and associated diving equipment to recover, inspect, repair, install, and remove devices from USN marine vessels and structures.

description:
Job description:
Admin Assistant:
About the Role:
TIMBERTEK is a Dubai-based wood flooring company specializing in solid wood flooring installation, restoration, maintenance, sanding, and polishing for premium residential and hospitality projects.
We are looking for a proactive and detail-oriented Admin assistant to support our day-to-day operations, coordinate projects, and ensure smooth communication between clients, suppliers, and the internal team.
Key Responsibilities:
Oversee daily administrative tasks, including documentation, filing, and record management.
Coordinate schedules between the sales team, site team, and clients for installations, maintenance, and restoration projects.
Prepare quotations, invoices, and maintain payment records.
Maintain project documentation, service records, and job files.
Monitor inventory of flooring materials, finishing products, and tools, and coordinate replenishment with suppliers.
Assist the site team with scheduling, site access arrangements, and client follow-ups.
Respond to client enquiries via phone, email, and WhatsApp, and arrange site visits and quotation requests.
Maintain supplier and client databases, contracts, and related documentation.
Support general office administration, including attendance records and procurement of office and site supplies.
Prepare basic reports on project progress, service requests, and ongoing jobs.
Requirements:
Prior experience in the renovation or maintenance industry is essential.
Bachelor's degree or diploma in Business Administration or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
Minimum 2 years of experience in administration or office coordination, preferably within fit-out, interiors, flooring, maintenance, construction, or contracting.
Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple tasks and coordinate with clients, suppliers, and site teams.
Proficient in Microsoft Office and comfortable learning CRM, scheduling software, and AI tools to improve workflow.
Process-oriented with strong organizational and problem-solving skills.
Detail-oriented with a high level of accuracy.
Strong written English and communication skills.
Salary: AED 3000 per month
Work Arrangement:
This role is currently work-from-home. Depending on business requirements and performance, it may transition to a remote, hybrid, or onsite position in the future.

Join a collaborative and fast-paced team where your attention to detail, organizational skills, and ideas for improving processes will be valued and encouraged.

title: Expression of Interest
description:
Why we exist
We can get food, groceries and rides to our door on demand but accessing healthcare still means battling outdated systems, long waiting lists and travelling to sometimes overstretched clinical facilities.
Demand is rising, capacity in clinical settings is not coping, and patients' expectations of how they manage their health have fundamentally changed. That is why Heim exists: to build the AI layer for the last mile of healthcare, and make home the default place for patients to access care, at scale.
We surface and optimise unused practitioner availability, then work with healthcare providers to deliver care ranging from blood sample collection to wound dressing, reaching patients where and when they feel most comfortable.
About Us
We're a team of technologists, clinicians and commercial leaders with a track record of launching, scaling and exiting ventures in cloud technology and healthcare.
Before Heim, James Monico and Kelly Klifa built Testing For All, scaling the not-for-profit diagnostics provider into the go-to platform for Covid testing during the pandemic, testing over a million patients in under 18 months. Before that, James co-founded and scaled Cloudreach, exiting to Blackstone in 2017. Dr Elle Clarke, our Medical Director, is a fellow of the 2026 NHS Innovation Accelerator.
We've tripled our volume of appointments every period since going live at the end of 2023, and are backed by leading VCs in the space. We now cover 98% of the UK and hold a 4.9/5 patient rating.
Why we're asking
We're a small but mighty team and are growing quickly, which means roles open at short notice and close fast. Rather than lose good people to timing, we'd rather know who you are now. Tell us what you're interested in and we'll come back to you if and when something fits. Weâre building a picture of people across:
Clinical
Product
Technology
Growth & Commercial
Marketing
Operations & Delivery
HR and Finance
What We Look For, Whatever The Role
Extreme ownership and high velocity, paired with a real appreciation for clinical safety in a high-stakes environment
Low-ego collaboration across the whole organisation, engineers, commercial, clinical and implementation alike
Curiosity and initiative. You want to look under the hood, evaluate trade-offs and dig into the data rather than accept the first answer
A belief that there is beauty in simplicity, and a habit of returning to first principles on complex problems
A critical mind that guides the people around you towards clear decisions
Comfort with an unstructured, fast-moving environment, and readiness to be challenged
You never lose sight of the reality faced by nurses and patients out in the community
We're a small team and we get a lot of interest, so unfortunately we won't be able to come back to everyone. Your details stay on file, and if you're a fit for us, we'll be in touch!

title: Calling Specialist
description:
JOB DESCRIPTION
Thank you for showing interest in Outreach Specialist role at KSNL Consulting LLC! Before we move forward, we want to make sure you have a full picture of what we do and what this job actually looks like day to day.
Who we are : KSNL Consulting is a project consulting firm. Every day, thousands of commercial projects hits the portal we work from â Nature of the projects can be any project from changing a bulb to providing aircraft maintenance project. Our company stick to the practical, everyday services: commercial cleaning, landscaping, transportation, roof replacement, electrical, plumbing, and others like it. Our job is to match those projects with the right vendors and manage everything in between.
Your job : You'd be the person making that match happen. Here's how it works â we hand you a project summary with the location, frequency, required certificates, insurance, and materials. You take that summary, put it in your own words, and explain it to vendors over calls and texts. And here's the best part: you're not selling them anything. You're offering them business for work they already do.
On every first call, you'll need to do three things: explain the project, collect the vendor's cell number and business email, and lock in their site visit appointment. That contact info matters â all our follow-ups happen over text, and you'll follow up with each vendor at least 4 times.
The numbers : This is a high-volume outbound call role. You'll be making 150â200 calls a day, plus reaching out to project managers and contracting officers.
If that sounds like something you'd thrive in and you have the proficient in English Communication, then follow the STEPS.
STEP#1: Please send us a at least ONE MINUTE VOICE NOTE explaining your academic and professional accomplishments. Also do tell us about your journey. Also give us a good reason why you think you are the best candidate for this position. WhatsApp number +17032204299
STEP#2: Complete the Application Form and Trial Task given in this form ( follow the instructions ). and mail at ksnl.federal@gmail.com
https://docs.google.com/forms/d/1f32l5IiqhfqALYLH6gHwVBPHsDEdxyEZ67K-099xcW0/preview
STEP#3: Setup an interview call on CALENDLY by clicking this link . https://calendly.com/humanresource-ksnl/30min
FEW THINGS TO KEEP IN MIND
1. You will be connected on zoom, sharing your screen for the time allocated to work.
2. Your mic shall be UNMUTED at all times during 10 Hour working hours. 60 min of Break
3. NO BACKGROUND NOISE due to the fact THAT YOU WILL BE WORKING IN A GROUP SETTING AND CALLING VENDORS
4. This is a FULL TIME POSITION . No other job will be allowed .
Qualifications
Excellent English verbal and written communication skills
Experience in outboarding calling to North American and European Clients.
Experience in detailing high call volume approximately 150 - 200.
Able to understand complex project and explain in simple words.
Able to talk convincingly with the vendors and able to persuade the vendor for site survey.

title: Nanny Camp Hill
description:
Full-time Nanny, Camp Hill (40-hours), Commence ASAP!
Hours: MondayâFriday, approx. 40hrs per week (6amâ2pm) | Permanent Full-Time (4-day week may be considered for the right candidate)
Salary: From $70,000 + super + entitlements
Minis: Two boys, 4 & 2, with a baby girl due in November
Commence: ASAP
About Our Clients
This warm and vibrant Camp Hill family are looking for an easy going and friendly Nanny to become a valued part of their home. Dad is a busy business owner, while Mum is a stay-at-home mum preparing to welcome their third mini later this year. They value integrity, accountability and kindness, and have created a positive, respectful home where open communication and mutual appreciation are at the heart of family life.
Their boys are active, curious and full of laughter, enjoying swimming lessons, music, park adventures and playing with monster trucks. The family embraces a healthy lifestyle with limited screen time and loves outdoor play and learning through everyday experiences.
Duties
Sole charge of the minis when required
Planning fun, engaging outings and activities
Taking the minis to swimming, music and other social activities
Preparing healthy meals for the minis
Light household duties including kitchen tidying, dishes, rubbish and general wipe-downs
Driving the minis to activities using the family vehicle
Supporting the smooth running of the household during busy mornings
The perfect fit
You're reliable, adaptable and personable, with a genuine passion for supporting young families. You are known to be a nanny who is respectful and not overbearing and follows family routine whilst being confident working independently while respecting the family's routines and parenting style.
All you need is minimum 3-yrs professional childcare and or nanny experience, a valid Blue Card, police check, first aid/CPR certification and a current driver's licence. Most importantly, you'll be someone who builds trust naturally, communicates openly and enjoys creating a calm, fun and nurturing environment where children can thrive.
What's in it for you?
Become a genuinely valued and trusted member of a warm family
A supportive, respectful workplace where you'll be appreciated
Long-term, permanent employment providing stability and consistency
A nanny car for your job
Competitive salary plus superannuation and full entitlements
Opportunity to build meaningful relationships with three wonderful children as the family grows
If you have always dreamed about becoming a professional nanny with a natural gift bonding with children, we'd love to hear from you!
Apply Now
Hit Apply , or send your updated resume and introduction outlining why you'd be the perfect fit to hello@miniconnections.com.au . Shortlisted applicants will be contacted.

At Downer we plan, create and sustain. Downer is the leading provider of integrated services in Australia and New Zealand. Through trusted relationships and world leading insight we work closely with our customers to design, build and sustain assets, infrastructure, and facilities.
Looking for a hands-on role with career development opportunities? Whether you're starting out or already have experience in construction materials testing, we'd like to hear from you!

Laboratory testing of asphalt and construction materials
Field testing across a range of civil and infrastructure projects

Pavement coring and sample collection
Maintaining accurate testing records and results
Working on day and night shift rosters as required

Current P Licence minimum
A positive attitude and willingness to learn
Strong commitment to safety and quality
Ability to work both independently and as part of a team
Willingness to work outdoors and travel to project sites
Previous construction materials testing experience is advantageous but not essential
What's on offer:
Competitive hourly rate
Full training provided
Ongoing development and nationally recognised qualifications
Day and night shift opportunities
Supportive team environment
Long-term career opportunities within Downer
Important Information:
The successful applicant will be required to complete:
Pre-employment medical & physical assessment
Drug and alcohol testing
Ongoing compliance with Downer's Zero Harm safety standards
Reference Number: 735122
Apply now with your resume and a brief cover letter. For more information, contact Amy Isgar at highvolumerecruitment@downer.co.nz.
