Work from anywhere in Europe | SaaS
Awesome opportunity for a self-motivated and energetic people person to join our remote team and help sell our world-leading SaaS products, from anywhere in Europe.
We pay a great salary, based on experience and location. We don’t pay commissions, because good sales are a team effort—from engineering, to operations, marketing, and support, our high-performing team all contribute to a great product and service that our clients love. Everybody in the company is rewarded with a share of profit each December—we succeed together.
Our much-loved products are in demand and are proven to make a difference to our clients’ lives. You’ll be selling world-leading software through a well-considered process that leaves room for personal flair.
SaaS experience is extremely beneficial but strong communication skills, patience, curiosity, keenness to learn and friendliness are key to success in this role.
Join our Rebel Alliance
Creative Force is experiencing strong growth and as we scale our efforts in 2026 and beyond, we’re looking for enthusiastic individuals to join our diverse team of Jedis to help recruit new clients as they navigate the decision process, and transform them into long-term supporters.
You’ll be a respected member of our remote global sales team and will be well supported with the tools, knowledge and answers you need to provide exceptional levels of service, and to make the most from solid sales traction with our two in-demand products.
As you master the Force and the multitude of skills needed in this role, attracting clients to join our mission, you will be recognised and rewarded with strong career and salary progression.

Help prospects find the specific value they seek (this is the product you are looking for)

title: Risk & Compliance Specialist
description:
Why Polar?
It's never been easier to build, ship and scale software.
But it's never been harder to monetize it.
Modern startups look fundamentally different than prior generations:
Smaller teams
Exponential revenue growth relative to headcount
Higher variability in costs (LLMs) requiring more frequent pricing iterations
Laser focused on product development and distribution
Delegating and automating everything that is boilerplate â be it in their codebase or business operations.
Exceptional billing primitives, APIs and SDKs are essential, but delightful integration is not enough.
Startups need a billing platform designed for their speed of iteration. Combining billing and analytics in one platform to offer customer- and feature unit economics in real-time. Offering built-in pricing and cost insights, simulations and optimizations while simultaneously handling international compliance, tax management, fraud prevention and more.
That's Polar. We're building the next standard for applied AI startups.
Join our small, talented and engineering-led team across Europe as we build the infrastructure powering the next generation of software companies.
We focus on shipping at high velocity to serve startup founders scale their businesses. Everything else is secondary.
Role & responsibilities: What you will do
As a Risk & Compliance Specialist, you'll help protect the integrity of the Polar platform by reviewing merchants, identifying potential risks, and ensuring compliance with our policies and payment partner requirements. You'll partner closely with Merchant Support, Product, and Operations to balance a seamless merchant experience with effective risk management.
We're a small team, so you'll have the opportunity to do more than review accounts. You'll help improve our processes, identify emerging risk trends, and shape how Risk Operations scales as Polar grows.
You'll work with the team to:
Review new merchant applications and assess eligibility to sell on the Polar platform.
Conduct ongoing account reviews to identify changes in merchant activity or risk profile.
Evaluate merchants for compliance with Polar's Acceptable Use Policy and other platform requirements.
Investigate fraud, payment risk signals, disputes, chargebacks, and other suspicious activity.
Manage merchant offboarding, payout holds, and other risk-mitigation actions as needed.
Partner with payment providers and internal teams to resolve compliance and account-related issues.
Document review decisions and maintain clear, consistent internal processes.
Identify opportunities to improve risk workflows, tooling, and operational efficiency.
Monitor emerging abuse trends and escalate complex or high-risk cases to leadership.
What we're looking for
We're looking for someone who enjoys solving complex problems, making thoughtful decisions, and protecting the platform's integrity. You're analytical, detail-oriented, and comfortable working with ambiguity while balancing merchant experience with compliance requirements.
You have excellent judgment, communicate clearly, and can explain difficult decisions with empathy and professionalism.
Skills & Experience
2+ years of experience in Risk Operations, Trust & Safety, Compliance, Fraud Operations, Payments, or Merchant Operations.
Strong analytical and investigative skills with exceptional attention to detail.
Excellent written communication skills and the ability to explain complex decisions clearly and professionally.
Experience reviewing accounts, investigating fraud, or evaluating merchant risk.
Ability to prioritize competing priorities and make consistent, well-reasoned decisions.
Comfortable working cross-functionally with Support, Product, and external payment partners.
Familiarity with SQL for investigating data, validating risk signals, and answering operational questions is a plus.
90-day Plan & Milestones
First 30 Days - Learning
â Learn Polar's products, merchant onboarding flow, and Merchant of Record model.
â Become familiar with the Acceptable Use Policy, internal review guidelines, and risk workflows.
â Shadow merchant reviews, investigations, and offboarding processes.
â Begin reviewing low-risk merchant applications with guidance.
First 60 Days - Implementing
â Independently review new merchant applications and ongoing account reviews.
â Investigate fraud signals, disputes, and payment risk cases.
â Manage standard offboarding cases and payout holds.
â Start contributing to improvements in documentation and review processes.
First 90 Days - Contributing
â Own merchant reviews from initial assessment through final decision, ensuring every case is well documented and consistently applied.
â Handle more complex risk and compliance cases.
â Identify trends and recommend operational improvements.
â Partner with Product, Support, and Operations to improve workflows and the merchant experience.

Payroll is broken. Come fix it alongside a team thatâs as passionate as you are!
At Check, weâre not just building our own business â weâre building payroll businesses together with every one of our partners. As the inventors of embedded payroll, weâre redefining how people get paid and making it easier for payroll businesses to launch, grow, and thrive.
On our team you'll use creative problem-solving, critical thinking, and grit to simplify the complexity of payroll for thousands of employers of every size, across all industries. We ignore conventional role boundaries in favor of the unique strengths and values each builder brings to our mission: make paying people simple .
Check out the full story
Tune in
Check is far more than just API infrastructure. Weâre a springboard for building and scaling payroll businesses.
The Support team plays a critical role in keeping payroll running for thousands of businesses and millions of workers by supporting the platforms that build payroll products on top of Check's infrastructure. When questions arise or something doesn't behave as expected, we investigate what happened, explain it clearly, and drive toward a solution.
This role sits at the intersection of payroll expertise and technical product knowledge, and the work is fast-moving, analytical, and highly investigative. A typical day involves untangling complex payroll scenarios, identifying root causes, partnering across the company to solve problems, and communicating clearly with partners whose payroll expertise may range from seasoned professionals to first-time operators. Along the way, you'll develop deep expertise in Check's platform, payroll operations, and the broader payroll ecosystem while building trusted relationships with the partner teams you support.
Support sits at the center of Check's product ecosystem. We work closely with Engineering, Product, Tax, Risk, and other teams to troubleshoot issues, surface product insights, and improve the platform. Few roles offer the same visibility into how modern payroll infrastructure operates at scale. If you enjoy solving layered problems, asking thoughtful questions, and translating technical concepts into clear, actionable guidance, you'll thrive here.
In This Role, You Will
Provide exceptional partner support. You'll manage a high volume of partner requests, primarily through written communication, balancing urgency with thoughtful investigation while consistently meeting or exceeding SLAs.
Investigate complex payroll problems. You'll dive deep into payroll and tax questions, break issues into manageable pieces, trace root causes through our systems, and drive issues toward resolution with accuracy, curiosity, and ownership.
Collaborate across the company to resolve issues. You'll partner closely with Engineering, Product, Tax, Risk, and other teams to troubleshoot issues, escalate bugs, and help drive solutions that unblock partners quickly.
Surface patterns and improve the system. You'll identify recurring partner questions, operational friction points, and product trends, surfacing insights that improve documentation, workflows, and product behavior.
Build trusted relationships. Whether youâre working with experienced payroll professionals or teams who are brand new to the industry, youâll build trust by bringing empathy, ownership, and transparency to every interaction and explaining technical or operational issues in ways they understand.
Escalate thoughtfully. Youâll exercise careful judgment about how and when to pull others in on a problem or escalate upward, and youâll ensure everyone has clear context so they can quickly understand the problem and help identify a path to resolution.
Deliver service that feels personal. Youâll build lasting relationships with our partners by developing a deep understanding of their platforms and the businesses they serve. Youâll establish yourself as a reliable and trusted resource by making people feel heard, helped, and valued.
Many backgrounds could fit this role, but ideal candidates will have most or all of the following:
2+ years in a client- or partner-facing role, supporting customers, partners, or technical products.
1+ years working at a payroll provider, payroll platform, HR technology company, fintech company, or in a role that required applying payroll knowledge to solve customer problems
Experience balancing multiple priorities in a fast-paced support or operations environment
Strong investigative instincts and genuine curiosity to understand not just what happened, but why
Exceptional attention to detail and the ability to maintain accuracy while solving complex problems
Comfortable collaborating across technical, operational, and administrative teams to solve partner problems and enable new business capabilities
Excellent written communication skills with the ability to explain complex technical or operational concepts clearly and empathetically
Experience using ticketing or case management systems (Zendesk preferred)
Willingness and availability to attend our annual 3 day company offsite each spring
Travel & Office Policy
The Check team is distributed across the US. Roles can be remote, hybrid, or based in one of our offices in New York City or San Francisco . We offer ample opportunities and encourage employees to attend team offsites, events, and hackathons throughout year. All Checketeers gather in the spring for our annual 3-day company retreat.
For our in-office and hybrid employees, our offices are open all week. We provide meals on Tuesdays and Thursdays and there are regular happy hours, game nights, and other in-person events.
Remote work at Check requires the ability to perform all responsibilities without distraction or disruption, while maintaining quality, effective communication, and productivity.
Check is proud to be an Equal Opportunity employer. We do not discriminate based on race, religion, color, national origin, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, gender expression, transgender status, sexual stereotypes, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, or other applicable legally protected characteristics. We also consider qualified applicants with criminal histories, provided they are consistent with applicable federal, state, and local laws. Check is committed to providing reasonable accommodations for candidates with disabilities in our recruiting process.
Check participates in E-Verify and will provide the federal government with Form I-9 information from all new employees to confirm that they are authorized to work in the U.S. Check does not use E-Verify to pre-screen applicants.

title: Assistant Area Sales & Customer Manager
description:
Role Title: Assistant Area Sales & Customer Manager
Function: Customer Development
Location: Mumbai RO
Reporting to: Consumer Cluster Head
Here is how your day at Unilever would look like:
Customer Infrastructure & satisfaction: The ASCM is responsible for ensuring a robust Customer Infrastructure is in place in the territory. Distributors are appointed by the ASCM wherever necessary, and it is his/her responsibility to track their overall performance on key metrices. ASCM is supposed to optimize the quantity & quality of customers in his area such that there are no service gaps while ensuring adequate service levels for trade and financial viability for customers. She/He monitors the financial health and profitability of all Customers. The ASCM also needs to step in from time to time to resolve customer issues which cannot be handled at a field-force level. Along with his/her team (FF) the ASCM is also responsible for primary & secondary customer complaint resolution.
Growth & Execution: The ASCM drives Top-line growth in the area and ensures all execution metrices are also in place. She/He will also need to monitor channel-wise and category-wise growths in the territory. It is also the ASCMâs responsibility to ensure all new launches are landed in the area and to ensure all merchandising activities are run well. Execution metrics are the input metrics for delivering share gaining growth and are hence very important.
Drive a team: Team handling & team building are the most important aspects of an ASCMâs role. An ASCM is responsible for managing the team, motivating them and getting them to deliver their metrices. She/He needs to understand the working style and strengths and weaknesses of each person to get them to reach their potential and also needs to provide developmental inputs on a continuous basis. How an ASCM binds his/her team together is often a make-or-break factor in performance of a team.
Liaising with key Partner Functions: The ASCM liaises with the Supply Chain Team to ensure pack wise estimates are built correctly for the area. She/He also ensures norms build up at an RS level are hygienic and supplies from depots are in order. She/He also ensures that the stock build up at Customer points are at the acceptable level. The ASCM works with the Commercial Team to ensure customers are healthy and that payments to company are in order.
Ensuring controls & financial hygiene: Along with Commercial & Supply Chain team, ASCM is supposed to have check on system hygiene at customers on aspects like extent of sales return, extent of damage/ shortage claims, mismatch between primary & secondary, physical vs. book stock mismatch, trade discount
hygiene etc. ASCM needs to play an active role in probing cases of deviation from norms on the above-mentioned aspects.
Key Skills & Requirement
MBA with relevant experience.
Analytical skills and demonstrated ability to manage the business by the numbers.
Jobs involving quick decision making.
Jobs involving extensive oral communication, people interaction & negotiation.
Experience in a highly analytical, results-oriented environment. Preferably FMCG.
External customer interaction.
Experience of jobs involving active listening skills, highly consultative and solutions oriented.
Deep understanding of the retail and wholesale landscape in India with prior interactions with sellers and distributors is desirable.
Experience in selling new products and developing markets.
All official offers from Unilever are issued only via our Applicant Tracking System (ATS). Offers from individuals or unofficial sources may be fraudulentâplease verify before proceeding.

title: Marketing Coordinator Partner Programs
description:
Overview
Digiday Media is looking for a Marketing Coordinator, Partner Programs to lead the marketing and fulfillment of sponsored programs across four premium media brands.
Who you are
You have about a year of experience in media and/or growth marketing and are eager to take on more responsibility. Youâre a pro and extremely reliable when it comes to managing projects and ensuring theyâre executed on time and at a high level. Youâre analytical and when it comes to solving problems, youâre able to use data to identify trends and challenges and turn those into action items. Youâre results-oriented and are extremely ambitious and motivated when it comes to delivering on those results. Most of all, youâre able to work extremely effectively across teams to be able to deliver results for our partners.
Responsibilities
Oversee the fulfillment and marketing for partner programs, including webinars, white papers, reports, surveys, guides and more. Youâll be responsible for developing promotional plans for each of these programs and executing them at an extremely high level.
Coordinate the distribution and promotion for each program. Youâll manage a content calendar and be responsible for using various channels across the company to promote each of these assets.
Report on the progress and success of each campaign. From a fulfillment standpoint, youâll keep key stakeholders informed of the progress of each campaign and make recommendations to improve performance. From a promotion standpoint, youâll track the success of the tactics being used and make recommendations in order to optimize those tactics going forward.
Work closely with client service and custom content teams to coordinate the logistics of campaign launches.
Work with the sales team on feasibility for RFPs and other programs being pitched. Youâll work closely with vp, marketing & growth to ensure all programs are sold in a way that puts Digiday Media and our partners in position to be successful.
Requirements
About one year of experience (internships count)
Media, marketing or communications background preferred. Ideally, a mix of the three.
A proven ability to manage a number of projects at once. Youâre extremely organized and can juggle multiple campaigns in your sleep.
Experience with direct response channels. Ideally, working with email marketing, display advertising, social platforms and/or other native publishing placements.
A willingness to âroll up your sleevesâ. Youâre happy to get your hands dirty and get s**t done.
Comfortable in a fast-paced, occasionally ambiguous environment
Meticulous attention to detail. Nothing gets by you.
Generally fluent in marketing technology
ABOUT DIGIDAY MEDIA
Digiday Media is a vertical media company founded in 2008 by our Chairman, Nick Friese. Our mission is to chronicle how industries like media, marketing and retail are navigating change.
Our approach is to continually reimagine and reshape the media we create and the way we connect the industries we cover, guided by our core virtues of quality, honesty, curiosity and tenacity.
OUR BRANDS
Digiday: The home of modern media and marketing.
Glossy: Chronicling the evolution of beauty and fashion.
Modern Retail: Exploring the transformation of the retail industry.
OUR VALUES
Be respectful. We work with each other in a way thatâs empathetic, kind and productive.
Embrace change. Media is perpetually changing. To keep up, so are we.
Choose quality. Quality over quantity -- always.
Experiment. Weâre obsessed with finding ways to get better.
Be honest . Whether itâs the way we report on the industries we cover or how we work together, it starts with honesty.
OUR BENEFITS
Remote work schedule flexibility. Work from where you want: home, the moon -- it's up to you.
Professional development : We help pay for approved courses and training to help you grow.
Generous paid time off . Including half-day Fridays, a week off following Christmas and ample PTO.
Insurance including health, vision, dental and 401k.

title: Program Delivery Officer Level 1
description:
In this role you will ensure a high level of community safety through the delivery of approved general and /or sexual offending programs to those offenders assessed as requiring offender intervention programs.
Mandatory Requirements
The following mandatory requirements apply to this role:
The possession of a tertiary qualification in preferably in psychology, social work, education or behavioural sciences, however, other Bachelor degrees may be considered at the discretion of the recruitment panel in consultation with Offender Rehabilitation and Management Services.
Membership or affiliation with a relevant professional association will be highly regarded
PDO specialising in the delivery of sexual offending programs you will be provided with training in the use of relevant assessment tools (STATIC-99 and STABLE-2000) to allocate sex offenders to appropriate treatment.
The primary accountabilities of the Program Delivery Officer (Level 1) include:
Participate in planning activities to ensure offenders have timely access to appropriate programs and interventions
Prepare offenders for offender intervention programs
Ensure offender program activities are consistent with evidence-based practice
Deliver offender intervention programs in accordance with operational plans
Provide advice to relevant officers regarding offender program suitability and/or other interventions
Monitor progress of offenders during programs and related activities and report on progress
Comply with program management procedures, standards and guidelines
Identify and respond appropriately to risks arising from offender management
Maintain own level of knowledge of contemporary offender programs research and practices, and legislation, policy and procedures in relation to offender management
Participate in case management activities as required for offenders assessed as requiring program participation
Provide timely information to relevant sites in relation to each offender's participation in programs for case management
Monitor offender management files and programs to ensure continuity and consistency
Ensure records and information data for the Integrated Offender Management system (IOMS) are accurate and current
Administer appropriate assessments to offenders
Analyse assessment results and record information
Contribute to case management and sentence management activities for offenders
Ensure records and information data for the Integrated Offender Management system (IOMS) and the Offender Programs Assessment Service (OPAS) are accurate and current
Ensure maintenance, accuracy and appropriateness of records and intervention reports, program data for appropriate authorities
Ensure the timely provision of advice to courts, boards and other agencies regarding offenders
Provide program impact reports to courts and parole boards for participants
Promote value of offender programs to relevant agencies and support services
Develop productive relationships with service providers and the community generally to enhance the community's regard for offender programs
The role description provides the minimum requirements for the role. The incumbent may be required to undertake other duties as required outside of these primary accountabilities.
Applications to remain current for 12 months.
Occupational group Psychology, Counselling & Social Work

title: Compatibility
description:
CompatibilityWorking at Stripe is not for everyone
Not everyone finds success at Stripe. Those who do tend to share a few things in common.
The right people donât always think theyâre right
Successful Stripes are rigorous thinkers who appreciate that things worth doing are rarely simple. We want people who are not afraid to be wrong, who can enthusiastically back proposals they initially opposed, and who know how to support decisions with numbers and narrative. We operate in situations of substantial uncertainty and cannot afford either timidity or recklessness.
The global financial system can seem like a mystifying domain. It isnât. Itâs made of people and computers, like many other systems youâve worked on. Most Stripes donât come from finance, and theyâve thrived by bringing fresh perspectives. We want generalists who can parachute anywhere into our operations, learn a new field quickly, and execute competently beyond their formal remit.
We know that we canât be successful without nurturing the careers of both generalists and experts. People who thrive in high-conflict work environments often do not enjoy the experience here. We try to embrace kindness while still encouraging Stripes to take measured risks and act boldly, even in the absence of consensus.
Who is Stripe for?
Ambitious builders
Weâre building solutions without clear precedent, solving problems with far-reaching consequences. The people here find that energizing, preferring the joy of discovery to the comfort of certainty.
Adaptable problem solvers
AI is changing how the global economy works, how our customers work, and how Stripes work. The people who thrive here adapt quickly and treat obstacles as opportunities.
Rigorous thinkers
We argue from first principles, question assumptions, and donât stop at good enough. At Stripe, craft isnât a nice-to-haveâitâs the standard.
The most successful Stripes are the people who have the intellectual horsepower, the curiosity to learn a very complicated business, and the humility to get up every day and realize thereâs a huge amount of things they donât know.
Conor McNamaraHead of EMEA
What all Stripes have in common
Weâre dedicated to our work and optimistic about the world. We believe entrepreneurship and free markets do good, and building what supports them matters. If thatâs you, read on.
Motivated by our mission
Stripe is on a mission to grow the GDP of the internet.
Ask Yourself:
Do I see free markets and entrepreneurship as powerful forces for advancing progress?
Does enabling entrepreneurship and helping to unlock the internet economyâs full potential seem like a compelling use of my time and talents?
Embody our operating principles
âUsers firstâ is a cornerstone principle. Our users trust us to provide an essential service, and itâs a heavy responsibility that we take very seriously.
Ask Yourself:
Am I motivated to move mountains to protect and support businesses that depend on Stripe?
Am I driven to overcome obstacles and take on big things to drive progress, or do I feel overwhelmed by the sheer scale and breadth of sometimes nebulous opportunities?
Energized by change
The pace of change at Stripe and in the broader economy is accelerating. Youâll work outside your domain, take on problems that didnât exist a year ago, and be expected to adapt as quickly as the world does.
Ask Yourself:
Do I see a fast-moving environment as an opportunity rather than an obstacle?
Am I comfortable taking on problems outside my domain or experience?
Collaborative, multidisciplinary work
Building programmable financial infrastructure from first principles is inherently complex. It means that everything we create requires deep, collaborative, multidisciplinary work: technically, organizationally, and geographically.
Ask Yourself:
Am I excited by navigating complexity at scale?
How we operate
Youâll bring high standards to everything you do and find others who do the same.
Users first
We serve millions of businesses and a meaningful fraction of global GDP. We have a weighty responsibility to those businesses and to society. We work backwards from our usersâ needs, indexing especially on feedback from the most innovative. Everyone at Stripe talks to users.
Create with craft and beauty
With careful thought, anything can be made surprisingly great. Across every part of Stripe, we are committed to doing so. Well-crafted work indicates care for the user, and beautiful work indicates care for the world.
Move with urgency and focus
We move with speed on what matters most and take the time to invest in what will make us faster tomorrow. Whereas many companies get slower until theyâre eventually mired in mediocrity, we aspire to become the worldâs fastest company.
Collaborate egolessly
We work as one team: no fiefdoms, no hoarding information, no ânot my problem.â We question assumptions, debate energetically, and abandon ideas when better ones emerge. Weâre generous with credit and stingy with blame. We learn from mistakes together.
Stay curious
Stripe is an applied exercise in learning about how businesses tick and how the world works. Since the details and possibilities are infinite, we are always seeking to learn. Weâre energized by the unfamiliar, preferring the joy of discovery to the comfort of certainty.
Obsess over talent
Itâs every Stripeâs responsibility to help hire the best and to push for excellence everywhere. Managers must relentlessly uphold our high talent bar, lead their teams with clarity and context, foster development, and ultimately support Stripes in accomplishing the best work of their careers.
Our culture
Like all great workplaces, Stripe has its own working culture, with norms that can surprise, delight, and occasionally perplex.
Friday Fireside
Friday Fireside is a weekly Stripe-wide forum hosted by Patrick and John. We hear from a Stripe user and get their unvarnished feedback, invite Stripes to chat about (or demo!) their recent work, and welcome external experts to discuss timely and relevant topics.
Convergence
Every December, Stripes come together for Convergenceâa full-day event and Stripe tradition dating back to 2014. Itâs a chance to reflect on the past year, hear about our priorities for the next year, learn from each other, and poke fun at ourselves.
How we show up in the world
Cheeky Pint
Ideas meet the pub hang. In this podcast series, John Collison sits down with founders, builders, and leaders to discuss their craft over a pint.
Watch Cheeky Pint
Stripe Press
Stripe Press publishes books about ideas for economic, technological, and scientific progress. We print works we think can be broadly useful.
Find Stripe Press titles
Works in Progress
Stripeâs online and print magazine focuses on scientific, technological and economic advancement.
Read about Works in Progress
Frontier
Launched in 2022, Frontier is Stripeâs advance market commitment to buy an initial $1.8B of permanent carbon removal by 2040.
Learn about Frontier
Intercept
A new initiative focused on dramatically reducing the burden of respiratory viruses.
Learn about Intercept
Frequently asked questions
What is it actually like to work at Stripe day to day?
Fast-paced, intellectually demanding, and creative. The volume is high, and the problems are high stakes. But you wonât be doing it aloneâwe work with egoless collaboration. Most Stripes will tell you the caliber of their teammates is one of the things they value most, and that it raises their own standard of work.
How does Stripe invest in your growth?
Through the work itself, mostly. Stripe gives people stretch projects early, which means youâre solving problems that are hard and consequential to the business. Beyond that, we offer mentorship, direct feedback, and an annual education stipend for courses, conferences, and resources that move your career forward. The expectation is that youâll grow quickly here. Weâre set up to support you.
How does AI shape the work here?
AI is embedded in how everyone at Stripe builds, analyzes, and operates. Engineers use AI tools daily to accelerate development. Teams across product, design, and operations are building AI-powered features for the businesses and consumers who rely on Stripe. We think carefully about where AI creates real value versus where it introduces risk.
What does it mean to do your best work here?
Stripe is a place to do career-defining work. The stakes are high: millions of businesses rely on Stripe. Itâs a responsibility that requires combining urgency with high standards, an often demanding mix. In exchange, you'll have the support and opportunity to pursue big ideas and change how things work, with a high degree of autonomy.
More on careers at Stripe
Get our perspective on why what we build matters.
Opportunity
Start your career at the center of the global economyâsee what we offer for early career opportunities.
Emerging talent
Weâre hiring. Explore our open roles and submit your application.
Open roles

title: Menu
description:
As Abraham Lincoln once said, âThe best way to predict the future is to create it.â If you want to advance your career but donât know where to start, here are some things you can do to get promoted at work.
By Michele Reynolds
Be a Model Employee
Rule number one for being a good employee is to always be on time and ready to go. Even if you work in a culture that runs behind schedule, itâs better to be on timeâor even earlyâeach day and to every meeting.
If youâre leading the meeting, show up with an agenda and be an active timekeeper. Itâs a sign that youâre organized, respect peopleâs time, and serve as a role model to peers. At the end of the meeting, give a quick recap and identify next steps.
Solve Problems, Donât Just Identify Them
One of the best ways to stand out as a budding leaderâregardless of your current roleâis to be self-sufficient and demonstrate solid judgment. Doing so wonât just set you apart as a critical asset to your team but also serve as a tactic to further develop your leadership skills. A helpful mantra is, âBe a problem solver, not a problem identifier.â
When you raise an issue to your boss, also propose a solution. Busy leaders often get bogged down by solving every problem their team faces. Do your boss a favor and find workarounds rather than just surface issues.
Respect Your Bossâs Time
Be considerate of your bossâs time. Before asking for help, consider the level of urgency and try solving the problemâor at least brainstorm a plan of action to run by your manager. Making an attempt first will demonstrate you know how to take initiative.
For things that require your bossâs intervention but arenât time-sensitive, keep a running list of items to discuss. Ask if you can get some time on your managerâs calendar and outline what youâd like to discuss in your meeting invite so you both come prepared.
Donât Be a Squeaky Wheel
Perhaps most important is a can-do attitude. Anything you can do to minimize your bossâs workload will likely benefit you in the long run. You can help by volunteering to take on something new or brainstorm solutions when a crisis pops up.
Baseball great Wade Boggs once said, âA positive attitude causes a chain reaction of positive thoughts, events, and outcomes. Itâs a catalyst, and it sparks extraordinary results.â
So, whatever you do, donât be a whiner. Even if youâre feeling stressed, save your venting for a friend and present a positive front to your boss.
Serve as a Vault
Earn trust by keeping information about confidential or sensitive subjects to yourself. Beyond that, donât gossip or backstab at the water cooler. By being a stand-up employee, youâll earn trust and respect.
Make Your Boss Look Good
Staying organized and moving quickly can make you, and your boss, look good. But donât move too fast. Getting things done efficiently is important, but quality matters, too.
Ensure your work represents your company well. If you take on additional responsibilities, confirm they align with whatâs expected of you. Your work reflects on your boss, so make sure theyâre proud of you and your product.
Ask for Advice
It may seem counterintuitive, but asking your boss for advice can yield dividends. According to research (pdf) by Harvard Business School Professor Alison Wood-Brooks, âIndividuals perceive those who seek advice as more competent than those who do not.â
Timed right, asking your boss for guidance can work to your advantage.
Speak Up
As Aristotle said, âThereâs only one way to avoid criticism: Do nothing, say nothing, and be nothing.â Since youâre reading this article, you clearly want to stand out, so speak up.
Confidently sharing your views and expertise in conversations or meetings allows you to demonstrate your knowledge and skills. You can also make an impression on your colleagues and superiors.
Project Confidence
Being a strong communicator is more than what you say. How you say itâboth in your body language and tone of voiceâmay matter more than the words themselves.
Albert Mehrabian, a professor at the University of California, Los Angeles, and an expert in nonverbal communication, proved through his research that what you say is negligible compared to how you say it. Body language and inflection matter more.
âNonverbal elements are particularly important for communicating feelings and attitude, especially when theyâre incongruent: If words and body language disagree, one tends to believe the body language,â Mehrabian told the site Right Attitudes.
That said, you can look like a leader through confident body language, such as your posture, stance, handshake, eye contact, and smile.
Advance Your Education
What else can you do to propel your career growth? If you want to sharpen your skills but donât have the time or resources to go back to school full- or even part-time, consider taking an online course.
According to HBS Professor Das Narayandas, thereâs a plethora of options that can benefit you and your employer.
As Narayandas said to the Harvard Business Review , âThe good news is that the growing assortment of online courses, social and interactive platforms, and learning tools from both traditional institutions and upstartsâ¦offers a solution. [Theyâre] flexible and immediately accessible, and it enables employees to pick up skills in the context in which they must be used. In effect, itâs a 21st-century form of on-the-job training.â
There are many affordable online business courses that can work around your schedule. Your employer might even cover the cost.
One to consider is Leadership Principles. It features interactive exercises to help you if youâre an early- or mid-career professional preparing for a leadership role.

title: Service Locator
description:
Building a sustainable tomorrow
KierBAM are a Joint Venture (JV) partnership between Kier and BAM UK & Ireland - BAM UK & Ireland's infrastructure segment is currently delivering the redevelopment project at a Royal Navy site located in Plymouth and we are seeking an experienced Service Locator.
The Service Locator will carry out the physical check and survey of all of the underground services within the area that is being investigated, the Service Locator will have the following responsibilities. You will use various geophysical techniques to locate the service, once they have been found, the services will be marked/spray painted onto the ground in the appropriate colour, defining the type and depth of the service. You will also maintain the contents of the permits on site, making sure the workforce remains compliant with conditions and processes outlined within the permits.
Due to the site being a high-security military naval base, additional security checks will be required a BPSS level of security clearance is necessary. These checks can take up to 8 weeks to process. Only candidates holding EU, NATO, 5 Eyes, or MISWG member passports and who have been UK residents for the last 5 years can be considered for this role. Your team
Location: Devonport Dockyard, Plymouth
Contract: Permanent, 42.5 hours a week Making Possible
In this role as Service Locator, you will be working in a live MOD facility. Your day-to-day tasks will include:
Authorise Permit to Break Surface
Ensure compliance with and enforcement of the project permit for the Break Ground procedure
Review method statements tailored to specific tasks
Mark all services within the work boundaries to protect colour standards
Provide teams with an overview of the services within their designated work boundaries and discuss methods for working around those affected services.

title: Chief Operating Officer
description:
Description
The Chief Operating Officer (COO) is the senior operational leader of U.S. Hunger, responsible for translating enterprise strategy into daily execution. This role owns P&L performance across all business lines â Full Cart, Hunger Projects, and the Data/Intelligence engine â ensuring the organization's earned-income model (97%+ of total revenue) operates with precision, accountability, and scalability.
The COO must bring the instincts of an entrepreneur and the discipline of a corporate operator: connecting dots others miss, asking tough questions that drive clarity, and building the systems that allow talented leaders to perform at their highest level. Operational excellence and mission-aligned impact are not in tension here â they are the same thing.
Enterprise Operations & P&L Execution
Own P&L execution across all business lines â each engine must meet its margin, revenue, and impact targets.
Establish and drive the operating cadence â monthly reviews, quarterly business performance reporting, and clear accountability across departments.
Make resource allocation decisions across competing priorities â deploying people, capital, and attention against the highest-value opportunities.
Present operational performance, capacity, and growth execution to the Board of Directors.
Partner with the CEO on scenario planning, structural growth strategies, and enterprise-wide decision-making.
Program Leadership â Full Cart & Hunger Projects
Provide executive oversight of Full Cart and Hunger Projects â ensuring delivery excellence, measurable outcomes, and scalability.
Partner with program directors to evaluate, evolve, and scale programs in response to partner needs, market opportunities, and operational realities.
Drive integration between program design, data infrastructure, and client-facing delivery â ensuring mission impact and revenue execution are operationally connected.
Oversee supply chain and logistics operations to ensure consistent, high-quality program delivery at scale.
Revenue Growth & Partner Execution
Own enterprise revenue execution across health plan partnerships, corporate engagement, and strategic growth opportunities â ensuring acquisition and retention targets are consistently met.
Drive strategies that deepen existing partner relationships and expand engagement across multiple service lines, maximizing long-term value and organizational sustainability.
Represent U.S. Hunger externally with payors, partners, and stakeholders â translating operational insight into compelling value propositions that differentiate USH in the market.
Leverage buyer-side CSR experience and existing relationships across the corporate social impact and food access ecosystem to accelerate partner acquisition and deepen engagement.
Cross-Functional Alignment & Executive Leadership
Partner with the Chief Technology Officer to define business requirements, program design priorities, and operational needs that shape the technology and data roadmap â ensuring platform delivery enables execution across all business lines.
Manage the VP of Finance & Enterprise KPIs and VP of People & Culture â two executives who maintain direct visibility to the CEO through their seat at the executive table â ensuring fiscal discipline, enterprise analytics, and workforce strategy are aligned with operational goals.
Actively contribute to organizational governance, strategy, and enterprise-wide decision-making as the CEO's primary operational counterpart.
Team Leadership & Development
Build, lead, and develop a high-performing operational leadership team â setting clear expectations, driving accountability, and coaching leaders who are growing into executive-level roles.
Develop performance metrics and accountability systems that connect individual and team outcomes to enterprise financial and impact objectives.
Promote a culture of rigorous inquiry, collaboration, and continuous improvement â where leaders are expected to think critically, challenge assumptions, and own their outcomes.
Foster an environment where staff understand both the business drivers of USH's earned-income model and the transformative impact of their work on the communities served.
These essential job functions are not to be construed as a complete statement of all duties performed. Employees will be required to perform other duties as required.
Requirements
10+ years of progressive leadership in operations, business management, or revenue execution â with direct P&L ownership.
Experience building, running, or scaling a business â including sales growth, client retention, and financial performance accountability.
Proven ability to lead and develop directors and VPs â coaching strong operators into executive-level leaders while holding them accountable to outcomes.
Demonstrated pattern of connecting dots across functions â seeing how operational, financial, people, and program decisions impact each other.
Experience at the board level â presenting performance, defending strategy, and engaging C-suite stakeholders directly.
Experience in mission-driven, earned-income environments where market discipline and social impact must coexist.
Strong communication across corporate, nonprofit, healthcare, and community sectors â direct, polished, and confident.
High emotional intelligence, with the courage to ask tough questions, the polish to challenge constructively, and the vision to see what's possible before it's obvious.
Background check is required for this role
Essential Physical Skills
Repetitive finger motion as used in computer use.
Extensive work with computer screens
Everyday requirements of bending, grabbing, holding, and lifting light objects
Work on Hunger Projects requires heavy lifting (up to 50 lbs), moving objects, pushing, and pulling, bending and kneeling
Up to 50% travel time

description:
Field Maintenance Technician â CTC-LIS
Location: Townsville, Queensland
Employment Type: Full time
About Cubic Defence
At Cubic Defence Australia, we deliver world-class training and simulation capability in support of the Australian Defence Force. Our teams help create and sustain technology solutions that support mission success, safety and readiness for those who serve.
About the Role
Reporting to the 2IC Field Services, the Field Maintenance Technician is responsible for supporting maintenance activities and ensuring the ongoing availability of Combat Training Centre â Live Instrumentation System (CTC-LIS) equipment. This hands-on role supports the preparation, deployment and maintenance of CTC-LIS Relay Stations, including diagnosis and repair of telecommunications equipment such as UHF, microwave and LTE systems, as well as basic servicing and maintenance of diesel-powered generators.
This position requires significant time deployed away from Townsville to various Australian Army and non-Defence training areas. During Force-on-Force exercise phases, you will work in a small team environment providing 24-hour maintenance coverage in the field.
Key Responsibilities
Conduct inspections, maintenance and associated repairs of CTC-LIS instrumentation and telemetry equipment.
Diagnose and repair telecommunications equipment, including UHF, microwave and LTE systems.
Conduct pre-deployment readiness checks of telemetry and mechanical equipment.
Maintain CTC-LIS equipment during field deployments.
Service and perform minor repairs to diesel-powered generators.
Provide technical advice and assistance during instrumentation function checking phases.
Be prepared to deputise for the 2IC Field Services during periods of absence.
Assume a leadership role within a small team environment during field deployments when required.
About You
You are a capable and motivated technician with strong fault-finding skills, sound communication ability and the confidence to work in both field and workshop environments. You are comfortable operating in dynamic conditions, prioritising maintenance issues and clearly communicating intent and outcomes.
Background and Experience
Experience in the installation and maintenance of communications systems.
Basic knowledge and understanding of electronics and electrical principles.
Proven fault-finding and problem-solving skills.
Ability to identify, analyse and prioritise maintenance issues.
Ability to work effectively in both field and workshop environments.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Experience using IT systems and programs.
Conditions of Employment
Certificate III in Telecommunications, Electrotechnology or a comparable qualification.
Clean Heavy Truck Licence to drive company equipment, or willingness to undertake training to obtain one.
Vehicle Loading Crane high risk licence, or willingness to undertake training to obtain one.
Work at Heights qualification, or willingness to undertake training to obtain one.
Forklift licence, or willingness to undertake training to obtain one.
Successful completion of a National Police Check.
Ability to obtain and hold an Australian Government Security Vetting Agency security clearance.
Working Environment
This role requires significant time deployed in the field and flexibility to support business operations across multiple time zones. From time to time, you may be required to monitor and respond to telephone calls, emails and other necessary communications from Cubic, customers or suppliers outside ordinary working hours to support critical issues or business needs.
Compliance and General Duties
Comply with the role job description and Cubicâs Quality Management System.
Follow Cubic Health, Safety and Environment policies and procedures.
Comply with established security policies and procedures.
Follow Cubic Human Resources procedures.
Perform other duties as requested.
Apply Now
If you are a technically skilled professional who enjoys hands-on work, problem-solving in demanding environments and supporting high-tempo military training exercises, we would welcome your application.
The description above is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all job duties, responsibilities and requirements.

title: Graduate Quality Officer
description:
Be part of a world-class team supporting vital Antarctic research and operations. The AIR Alliance brings together skilled professionals from Bouygues Construction Australia, The Australian Antarctic Division, Stantec and Mott MacDonald to deliver essential services in one of the most challenging and awe-inspiring environments on Earth. If youâre ready to push boundaries, work with cutting-edge projects, and make a real impact, this is your opportunity.
About The Role
The Quality Graduate supports the Alliance's quality management initiatives through quality assurance activities, compliance monitoring, audits, investigations, reporting, and continuous improvement projects. Working closely with stakeholders across the organisation, the role contributes to maintaining compliance with regulatory, contractual, and organisational requirements while supporting the effective operation of the Quality Management System. The Quality Graduate will assist the Quality Manager and Project Controls Manager with data analysis, auditing, risk management, and process improvement, while contributing to a culture of excellence and continuous improvement across the Alliance.
Key Responsibilities
Compliance with Alliance quality policies and procedures.
Timely completion of assigned quality activities and projects.
Accuracy and integrity of quality data and reporting.
Support the implementation and maintenance of the Quality Management System (QMS).
Assist in ensuring compliance with applicable standards, policies, procedures, and regulatory requirements.
Participate in document control activities, including the review and update of procedures, work instructions, and forms.
Maintain quality records, templates, registers, and controlled documents within the Alliance SharePoint quality management environment.
Support the development, maintenance, and delivery of the Alliance Internal Audit Schedule.
Coordinate audit logistics, track audit findings, and facilitate close-out of corrective actions.
Support continuous improvement initiatives using structured methodologies such as Lean, Six Sigma, or Kaizen.
Support implementation and verification of quality and compliance requirements associated with the Topside Program, including readiness activities leading to January 2027 delivery milestones.
Support review and implementation of Inspection and Test Plans (ITPs) and verify supplier compliance with agreed inspection and quality requirements.
Assist in monitoring supplier quality performance, documentation compliance, and adherence to Alliance quality requirements.
Support quality risk identification, assessment, treatment tracking, and reporting in accordance with Alliance risk management processes.
Coordinate and maintain records of mandatory quality training and inductions, including Quality Management Plan and Risk Management induction requirements.
Qualifications & Experience
Completion of a Bachelor's Degree in Engineering, Quality Management, Manufacturing, Science, Business, Supply Chain, Industrial Engineering or a related field.
Understanding of Quality Management Systems (ISO 9001 or similar).
Awareness of continuous improvement methodologies such as Lean or Six Sigma. Knowledge of audit principles and risk management concepts.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite, particularly Excel, Word, and Power BI (desirable)
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
High level of attention to detail and accuracy.
Ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines.
Bouygues Construction Australia values diversity and welcomes applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Australians.

title: Regional General Manager Airports
description:
Why WestJet
Since our story took off in 1996, WestJet has strived to enrich the lives of everyone in our world; a career with us is no exception. Weâre proud to be one of Canadaâs most admired and respected corporate cultures and continuously aim for the highest standards of service and success.
Join us, this is where your career story takes off.
This position is eligible for remote work, within Canada, under our mobile workforce program.
Regional General Manager, Airports
As the Regional General Manager, you will provide strategic leadership and direction to deliver safe operations while driving excellence in operational performance and guest service through our contracted service partners across the designated region. Reporting directly to the Vice President of Airports, you will lead a team of Regional Managers and collaborate closely with internal and external stakeholders to maintain regulatory compliance, foster positive relationships, and ensure a consistent, high-quality guest experience across all airport touchpoints within the region.
This role requires an experienced leader who holds service partners accountable for delivering WestJet's operational and service standards while balancing the needs of our guests, our partners, and our business. You will coach and support service partners in developing and executing airport action plans that address performance gaps, strengthen safety, and improve the guest experience.
The Regional General Manager will provide strategic oversight of airport operations across the region by identifying emerging risks, monitoring operational performance, and ensuring consistent execution of WestJet's standards and priorities. Through strong partnerships with service providers and airport authorities, you will drive continuous improvement, enhance operational resilience, and ensure our airports consistently deliver safe, reliable operations and an exceptional guest experience.
Key Deliverables Include
Foster a Safety Above All culture with Regional Managers by ensuring service partners achieve safety targets, monitoring performance trends, and addressing operational risks.
Lead, coach, and develop a high-performing team of Regional Managers to deliver operational performance, guest satisfaction, employee engagement, and financial results.
Provide strategic oversight of airport operations, ensuring consistent execution of WestJet's operational and guest standards and priorities.
Deliver regional operational performance by achieving operational, guest experience, and financial objectives while driving continuous improvement through station action plans.
Provide governance through audits, operational reviews, and performance assessments to ensure adherence to standards, identify risks, and drive corrective actions.
Analyze operational performance and safety data to identify trends and risks, inform operational decision making, prioritize resources, and strengthen oversight across the region.
Serve as the senior escalation point for Regional Managers, providing leadership and decision support for complex operational, guest, commercial, safety, and irregular operations.
Partner with the Strategic Procurement team to develop service partner strategies, support partner selection, and ensure service partners deliver safe, high-performing, and cost-effective operations.
Build and maintain executive relationships with airport authorities, service partner leadership, government agencies, bargaining agents, and other key stakeholders.
Lead regional operational planning to ensure airports are resourced and operationally ready for seasonal demand, network growth, start-ups, restarts, service partner transitions, station closures, and other strategic initiatives.
Champion innovation and continuous improvement by leveraging data and implementing initiatives that enhance operational performance, the guest experience, employee engagement, and financial results.
Participate as a member of the Airports Leadership Team to establish departmental priorities, contribute to strategic direction, and lead the development and execution of departmental initiatives.
Experience And Qualifications
3+ years Airports leadership experience required
Business leadership experience with a significant level of internal and external dependencies and relationships.
Possess strong business acumen to deliver departmental plans including budget.
Proven ability to multitask & handle changing priorities.
Confident in presenting materials and reports to the next 2 levels.
Post-secondary education with a business application an asset.
Ability to manage multiple leaders and locations simultaneously.
Proficient in PC based applications, Microsoft Project, Word, Excel and Outlook.
Ability to travel & spend time away for significant periods of time.
Project management skills considered an asset.
Knowledge of International regulations and guidelines (for example - TSA/Civil Aviation, UK High Commission etc.) an asset.
Proven track record of effectively influencing leadership teams via handling partners and developing strong direct leadership teams.
IATA SGHA experience would be beneficial.
The Benefits Of Being a WestJetter
WestJet provides all WestJetters with a competitive total rewards package. On top of that, we offer:
A fun and friendly culture with colleagues who work together to win
Travel privileges for you and your family, effective from your start date
Savings and Benefit programs that are flexible to meet your specific needs
Think weâre a great fit? Apply now!
About WestJet Group Of Companies
WestJet took to the skies in 1996 with just over 200 employees and three aircraft operating service to five destinations. Since then, WestJet has pioneered low-cost travel in Canada, cutting airfares in half, and increasing the flying population in Canada by more than 50 per cent. Since the Sunwing Airlines integration in 2025, more than 15,000 WestJetters support nearly 200 aircraft and connect guests to our global network of more than 100 destinations across North America, Central America, the Caribbean, Europe and Asia. The WestJet Group is a major Canadian employer and includes WestJet Airlines, WestJet Encore and Sunwing Vacations Group. Weâre Canadaâs leading value airline and largest vacation provider, with a united purpose of providing affordable and accessible air and vacation travel to Canadians.
Our safety promise
At WestJet, the safety and security of our people and our guests is a core value and at the heart of what we do. Safety and security are shared responsibilities all team members are expected to use safe work practices to ensure their well-being and the safety of others. WestJet recognizes that the use of Alcohol and Drugs can adversely impact a safe work environment and the well-being of others including guests, suppliers and the public, as well as place WestJet's operations at risk. All roles that are identified as Safey-Sensitive are required to pass a Pre-Employment Alcohol and Drug Test as per WestJet'sâ¯Alcohol and Drug Policy.â¯
Our commitment to diversity, equity and inclusion
We embrace what makes each of us unique, and what makes us uniquely WestJet. We welcome diverse skills, experiences and backgrounds so if you're passionate about this role, we encourage you to apply â even if you don't meet every qualification listed. WestJet is committed to inclusiveness, equity and accessibility throughout the selection process. If you require accommodation at any stage, please contact our Talent Acquisition team at talent@westjet.com.
We value the time and effort you put into your application. Our recruitment process is highly competitive and while every applicant will receive communication regarding their application status, only those selected to move forward will be contacted with next steps. If this role isnât the right fit, we encourage you to explore future opportunities with us.
About
For more information about everything WestJet, please visit westjet.com/aboutus.
If you wish to withdraw your application or request that your personal information be deleted, please contact us at talent@westjet.com.

title: Associate Events Social & Influencer Marketing
description:
POSITION OVERVIEW:
Society 18 is seeking a highly organized, creative, and proactive Associate of Events, Social & Influencer Marketing to support the agency's creator partnerships, experiential marketing initiatives, social media presence, and day-to-day operations.
This role is ideal for someone who thrives in a fast-paced environment, loves bringing ideas to life, enjoys wearing multiple hats, and is passionate about influencer marketing, social media, events, and creator culture. The Associate will work cross-functionally across events, social media, talent, partnerships, and operations while helping execute high-impact campaigns and experiences for creators and brand partners.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:
Social Media Marketing & Content Creation
Manage day-to-day content planning for Society 18's Instagram and LinkedIn channels.
Develop monthly content calendars aligned with agency campaigns, partnerships, creator announcements, and events.
Write engaging social media copy, captions, and assist with music selection for short-form content.
Design graphics in Canva, including creator announcements, milestone graphics, birthday posts, event promotions, partnership assets, and press announcements.
Film and edit Instagram Reels, creator spotlights, event recap videos, and partnership content using CapCut.
Maintain Instagram feed planning and overall visual consistency.
Schedule and publish content across social media platforms.
Publish Instagram Stories daily.
Engage with creators, brand partners, and community members through comments and direct messages.
Maintain creator posting trackers to ensure balanced representation across agency channels.
Develop quarterly newsletters and email marketing campaigns in Flodesk.
Create LinkedIn content highlighting agency partnerships, company milestones, leadership updates, and industry news.
Build and maintain creator pages on the Society 18 website.
Update creator biographies, follower counts, categories, and roster information as needed.
Event Production & Experiential Marketing
Assist with planning and executing creator dinners, networking mixers, brand activations, gifting experiences, industry events, and experiential campaigns from concept through post-event reporting.
Develop and maintain event production documents, including run-of-show schedules, timelines, itineraries, outreach trackers, and production checklists.
Research, source, and coordinate event venues, restaurants, and vendor partners.
Build and maintain agency venues and preferred vendor databases.
Coordinate pricing, proposals, availability, contracts, and logistics with vendors.
Support sponsorship outreach and assist in preparing partnership proposals and presentations.
Manage creator invitations, RSVPs, guest lists, and attendee communications using CreatorIQ, Partiful, Airtable, and Google Sheets.
Coordinate gifting logistics, product shipments, and vendor deliveries for events.
Prepare Independent Contractor Agreements (ICAs), NDAs, vendor agreements, and supporting documentation.
Organize event assets, contracts, invoices, presentations, production documents, and creative files in Dropbox.
Provide on-site event support, including setup, vendor management, guest check-in, production coordination, and event breakdown.
Capture behind-the-scenes photo and video content for real-time social media coverage.
Create post-event recap presentations in Canva and track creator coverage using Archive.
Influencer Marketing & Brand Partnerships
Pitch creators for brand activations, networking events, creator trips, fashion weeks, festivals, and industry experiences, including ESSENCE Festival, New York Fashion Week, Coachella, and other cultural moments.
Support creator onboarding by updating internal databases, website profiles, onboarding materials, and social media assets.
Assist with proactive creator pitching for paid brand partnerships.
Support talent scouting initiatives and maintain the agency's talent scouting database.
Research new creators, emerging trends, and partnership opportunities.
Executive & Administrative Operations
Coordinate meetings, calendars, and scheduling with creators, brands, vendors, and internal team members.
Prepare meeting agendas, capture notes, and distribute follow-up action items.
Maintain internal databases, presentations, production trackers, reporting dashboards, and operational documents.
Research and source brand contacts across beauty, fashion, travel, hospitality, wellness, food & beverage, and lifestyle industries using Apollo, Airtable, LinkedIn, and additional research tools.
Support day-to-day agency operations and assist with special projects as assigned.
QUALIFICATIONS:
Bachelor's degree in Marketing, Communications, Public Relations, Event Management, Business, or a related field (or equivalent experience).
1â3 years of experience in influencer marketing, social media, events, talent management, PR, or a related field.
Exceptional organizational skills with strong attention to detail.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously in a fast-paced environment.
Strong creative eye for branding, design, and social content.
Comfortable working both independently and collaboratively.

title: Growth Strategist
description:
About the Company
Why We Built Lyric: Supply chains are more critical and complex than ever. Every day, large enterprises navigate trillions of possible decisions that could impact the bottom line. Powerful algorithms and AI can address these problems, yet most organizations struggle to leverage supply chain AI at scale. The current SCM technologies are either rigid, limited-scope point solutions or custom solutions built in-house, which demand immense expertise and investment.
That isâ¦until now.
Enter Lyric : Lyric is an enterprise AI platform built specifically for supply chains, offering the best of both worlds:
Out-of-the-box AI solutions for optimizing networks, allocating inventory, scheduling routes, planning fulfillment capacity, promising orders, propagating demand, building predictions, analyzing scenarios, and more, plus
A platform-first approach that empowers both business and technical users with end-to-end product composability, leveraging no-code tools, their own code, or even forking our code to build and refine supply chain decision intelligence
With Lyric, enterprises no longer have to choose between flexibility and speed, they get both.
The Mission: Weâre building a new era in supply chain with the team best equipped to lead it. With over 20 years at the intersection of supply chain and algorithms, we developed a deep conviction that global supply chains needed something like Lyric. Since our inception in December 2021, that conviction has been validated time and time again.
Today, a growing number of Fortune 500 companies, including Smurfit WestRock, EstÃ©e Lauder, Coca-Cola, and more, are innovating on their own terms with Lyric. We canât wait to see what our customers, both current and future, are empowered to build with us next. Come build with us!
About the Role
Weâre hiring Growth Strategists: high-agency, client-facing professionals who will be the tip of the spear for Lyricâs go-to-market approach. This is not a traditional business development role. Youâll be embedded with senior sales leaders and cross-functional teams, opening new accounts while building real expertise in the enterprise GTM motion.
This role is designed for driven early-career professionals or post-MBA candidates looking to break into a high-growth startup. You donât need enterprise AI or supply chain experience, just the curiosity and work ethic to learn it fast.
Â
What Youâll Do
Identify, research, and develop new account opportunities across target verticals
Conduct outbound prospecting through multi-channel campaigns (email, phone, LinkedIn, events)
Shadow senior AEs and GTM leaders on client meetings and demos to build domain fluency and selling skills
Help prepare demo environments, RFP responses, and opportunity materials for active deals
Join opportunity teams to support key pursuit strategy and client engagement
Contribute to broader GTM activities: market research, competitive intelligence, event support, and content collaboration
Develop a point of view on target accounts and industries that sharpens the teamâs overall strategy
Who You Are
Early career (2+ years of professional experience) or post-MBA candidate looking to pivot into enterprise AI technology
Exceptional communicator; polished, articulate, and comfortable in client-facing settings
High agency: you take ownership, follow through, and donât wait to be told what to do
Intellectually curious with a hunger to learn about supply chain, technology, and enterprise sales
Strong researcher; you can quickly synthesize complex information and present it clearly
Resourceful with tools and technology. You're the kind of person who finds the right shortcut or AI-powered workflow to 10x your output before anyone asks you to
Collaborative and team-oriented; comfortable in a fast-moving, ambiguous environment
Â
Why This Role
Career path into AE, pre-sales, solution design, revenue operations, or other GTM roles
Direct mentorship from experienced Revenue leadership, VPs of Sales, and AEs. Youâll learn by doing alongside the best
You'll be helping define a new category, enterprise AI for supply chain, at a company where the playbook is still being written but the customer base already includes some of the largest, most complex enterprises in the world.
Join at a pivotal stage where your contributions are visible, and your growth trajectory is steep
Â
Even if you donât meet 100% of the qualifications, we recommend applying to the role!
Â
Location: Remote - Spain, Italy, Portugal. Some travel required.
Â
Compensation: We provide a competitive mix of salary, commissions, local benefits, and equity, designed to reward both your impact and growth.

Support customer metric forecasting, off-invoice trade events, planning tool inputs, and alignment between customer and internal systems.
Reconcile customer forecasts with NestlÃ© internal forecasts and support new item setup, trade management, and financial reconciliations.
Customer Distributor Support (10% of AA Role)

Prepare upcoming-period NRS materials and participate in monthly distributor touchpoints.
Resolve distributor-to-customer system connectivity issues and monitor out-of-stock reporting, sales impact, and follow-up communications.
Customer Account Team Support & Systems Administration (50% of AA Role)
Maintain customer forms, item data, product attributes, UPCs, dimensions, pricing information, and customer item management records.

title: Ship to Shore Technician
description:
Job Description
As a Ship-to-Shore Technician, you will play a vital role in supporting the safe and efficient operation of vessels arriving and departing at the port. This position involves working on the dock to ensure the proper mooring, securing, and release of ships, while maintaining safety and operational standards. In addition to mooring responsibilities, the role will also involve performing general maintenance and support tasks as required to ensure overall port and equipment readiness.
The Ship-to-Shore Technician is responsible for, but not limited to the following:
Docking and Undocking Operations
Assist in safely docking and undocking cruise ships at port using mooring lines, ropes, and related equipment.
Work in coordination with the shipâs captain, crew, and port authorities to ensure that vessels are safely secured and aligned with docking infrastructure.
Mooring Line Management:
Handle and manage mooring lines, ensuring they are properly fastened, tense, and released.
Perform visual inspection of mooring lines and related equipment regularly for wear and damage, ensuring everything is in safe working condition. (Regularly performed by ship crew)
Ship and Dock Safety
Maintain safety protocols during mooring procedures, ensuring that all tasks are performed in accordance with safety regulations.
Monitor weather conditions and report any changes that could affect docking or undocking procedures.
Communication and Coordination
Communicate effectively with other team members on board and shore-based personnel.
Work with the Port Authorities to ensure the timely and safe transfer of passengers and cargo.
Emergency Procedures
Be trained to respond in case of an emergency during docking or undocking operations, including accidents or hazardous situations.
Ensure all mooring operations are conducted efficiently and safely, even under adverse weather conditions or emergencies.
PPE Equipment (MANDATORY)
Must always be in possession of steel toe boots (or prescribed non-slip safety shoes), safety vest, hard hat, gloves, radio/communication device. (To be provided by Carnival)
Cleaning & Maintenance of Pier & Mooring Equipment & Fixtures:
Ensure all mooring equipment such as winches, ropes, and fenders are properly maintained and operational (through visual checks and inspections).
Gangway Inspections & Maintenance: Inspect gangway components for wear, corrosion, proper tension, secure connections, and smooth operation to ensure safe pedestrian access and functionality.
Fenders: Conduct visual inspections of pier fenders and associated hardware to identify cracks, deformation, excessive wear, or damage caused by vessel contact, and report deficiencies as needed.
Mooring Bollards: Regularly inspect mooring bollards for structural integrity, including corrosion, cracks, loose anchor bolts, foundation stress, and coating condition, to ensure safe vessel mooring.
Stanchions & Pier Fixtures: Inspect stanchions and associated components for corrosion, damage, misalignment, or instability, ensuring they remain secure and serviceable.
Ropes: Inspect ropes for wear, fraying, or damage, and verify they are properly positioned and suitable for continued use.
Mooring Equipment Maintenance: Perform minor maintenance and repairs of mooring equipment when necessary.
Pier & Dock Cleaning: Maintain clean, safe, and non-slip pier surfaces by removing dirt, salt, algae, stains, debris and other buildup by pressure washing and using prescribed cleaning equipment and solutions, along all designated cruise pier and trestle areas.
Cleaning Equipment Operation: Safely inspect, operate, and maintain cleaning equipment, including scrubbers and pressure washers, ensuring proper use, cleaning, and storage after each operation.
Additional Maintenance Support Activities
Perform minor maintenance support to technical teams including plumbing, electrical, masonry, carpentry, and HVAC functions.
Mandatory Training:
Maintain compliance with organizational requirements by attending and participating in all required company training sessions.
Lagoon Care
Perform maintenance/inspections of lagoon systems.
Education:
Education: High School Diploma.
Maintenance knowledge is preferred.
Certified Pool Operator (CPO) required within 6 months of employment start.
Three to Five years' experience working in a mooring or associated fields.
Essential Experience Required:
Must be physically fit. Must have strong customer service skills. Ability to work in an outdoor environment. Ability to multi-task and think critically. Previous work experience preferred. Prolonged periods standing and working outside. Must be able to lift, up to 50 pounds at times. All island employees must be physically able to participate in emergency lifesaving procedures and drills. Full use/range of motion of arms and legs as well as full visual, verbal and hearing abilities are required to receive and give instructions in the event of an emergency. Ability to read and write English to understand and interpret written procedures. This includes the ability to give and receive instructions in written and verbal forms and to effectively present information and respond to questions from guests, managers, and co-workers.

title: Legal Expert
description:
